# What is NodeMP

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/introduction/what-is-nodemp/

> NodeMP is multiplayer for BeamNG.drive. What it is made of and what happens when you join a server.

NodeMP is multiplayer for [BeamNG.drive](https://www.beamng.com/). Players join a server, drive on one map and see each other's cars.

## The parts

| Part | What it is | Who needs it |
|---|---|---|
| Launcher | A Windows program: signs you in, lists servers, updates the client mod and starts the game. | Every player ([Install the launcher](/players/install/)). |
| Client mod | `NodeMP.zip`, the part inside the game: other players' cars, chat, name tags. | Every player. The launcher installs it. |
| Server | `Node-Server`, the program players connect to. Runs on Windows, Linux and in Docker. | Whoever runs a server ([Run a server](/hosting/quick-start/)). |
| Plugins | What makes one server different from another: chat commands, rules, game modes. Most are written in Lua. | Whoever writes them ([Overview](/plugins/overview/)). |
| Account | A free account at nodemp.com: one name on every server. | Optional for players ([Your account](/players/sign-in/)). Hosts need it to get a server into the list ([Get listed](/hosting/registering/)). |

## What happens when you join

You pick a server in the launcher and join it. The launcher checks the client mod and your game files, downloads the server's mods you don't have yet and starts BeamNG.drive ([Join a server](/players/join/#join)). If joining fails, the reason is in a launcher notification ([When something breaks](/players/troubleshooting/)).

While you play, your game simulates your own car and sends its position to the server, and the server passes it on to everyone else ([A bad connection and VPNs](/players/connection/#lag-and-jumping-cars)).

---

# Install the launcher

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/players/install/

> How to install the NodeMP launcher for Windows, what it does on the first start, and how it installs the client mod and updates itself.

The launcher is the program you play NodeMP through: you sign in, pick a server and join. It also installs and updates the client mod, which runs inside the game.

## What you need

- Windows 10 or 11.
- BeamNG.drive 0.40, started at least once: its first start creates the game's user folder.

The launcher finds the game by itself. If it doesn't, point it to the game folder ([below](#the-launcher-cant-find-the-game)).

## Install

1. Download the installer from the [download page](https://nodemp.com/download).
2. Run it. The launcher installs for your Windows user only and needs no administrator rights.
3. Wait for the installer to finish. The launcher opens by itself.

:::caution[Windows warning]
The installer isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may say the publisher is unknown. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. To check the file, run `Get-FileHash .\NodeMP-Setup-*.exe` in PowerShell and compare the result with the SHA-256 on the download page.
:::

## The first start

A small window checks for launcher updates and loads the server list. Then the launcher asks you to sign in: click **Sign in with browser** or **Continue as Test Drive** ([Your account](/players/sign-in/)). The main window opens next.

Another window may open instead:

- *Connection lost*: the server list didn't load. Check your connection and click **Try again**. If you know a server's address, click **Continue without the list** and join [by address](/players/join/#join-by-address).
- *Technical work*: NodeMP is down for maintenance. If the end time is known, the window shows it in Moscow time. **status.nodemp.com** opens the service status page. The launcher checks again by itself; **Try again** checks at once.
- *Account banned*: see [Bans](/players/sign-in/#bans).

## The client mod

The client mod (`NodeMP.zip`) does everything inside the game: other players' cars, the chat, name tags, the session panel. The launcher installs it in `mods\multiplayer\` in the game's user folder (by default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BeamNG\BeamNG.drive\current\`). At startup and before every join, it checks the mod and downloads a new version if there is one. You don't need to copy the mod by hand.

:::caution[Close the game]
Don't start BeamNG.drive while the mod downloads: a running game holds the file, and the launcher can't replace it.
:::

If the check fails but a mod is already installed, the launcher warns you (*Client mod could not be updated*) and joins with the old version. The server decides whether that version will do.

To check the mod yourself, click **Settings → Game → Client mod → Check now**. The installed version is shown there too.

## Launcher updates

The launcher checks for updates at startup and before every join and downloads them in the background. An update installs when you click **Restart and update** or right before a join: the launcher restarts and continues the join in the new version. No update installs while you're on a server.

Set up updates in **Settings → Launcher → Updates**:

- **Check for updates automatically**: when off, the launcher doesn't check on its own, at startup or before a join. **Check now** in the version row checks by hand.
- **Download updates in the background**: when off, the launcher only tells you a new version is out and downloads it when you click **Update now**. A required update still installs before a join.
- **Update channel**: *Release* or *Beta*. Not every build has this row.
- **Go back to v…**: reinstalls the previous version from the cache if the new one gives you trouble. The row appears only when the cache holds one.

If the launcher can't update itself, download the installer from the [download page](https://nodemp.com/download) and install it over the current one.

## The launcher can't find the game

Open **Settings → Game**. The line under the heading shows what the launcher found: `Version` and the game's version, or what's wrong, such as `No Bin64\BeamNG.drive.x64.exe in this folder`.

If the game isn't found, click **Browse** and choose the folder that holds `Bin64\BeamNG.drive.x64.exe`. Or start BeamNG.drive once through Steam, close it and click **Find it**.

---

# Your account

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/players/sign-in/

> Why you need a NodeMP account, how to create one and sign in through your browser, playing without one in Test Drive, and bans.

You can play NodeMP with or without an account. With one, you have the same name on every server, and servers can check that it's really you. Without one, in Test Drive, NodeMP picks your name; some servers don't let guests in.

## Create an account

Create an account at [nodemp.com/register](https://nodemp.com/register). You need:

- a username: 3 to 24 characters, Latin letters, digits, hyphens and underscores;
- an e-mail address that isn't disposable: the confirmation link goes there;
- a password: 8 to 200 characters, not on lists of leaked or common passwords;
- two checkboxes: *I accept the Terms of Use and the Privacy Policy* and *I consent to the processing of my personal data*.

The account is created when you open the link in the e-mail. Hosts use the same account; there is no separate host account. If you forget your password, click **Forgot your password?** on the sign-in page; the reset link arrives by e-mail and is valid for one hour.

## Sign in to the launcher

The launcher doesn't ask for your password: you sign in on the website, in your browser.

1. In the sign-in window, click **Sign in with browser**. The launcher shows a sign-in code and opens nodemp.com.
2. Sign in on the site if you haven't yet. With two-factor authentication on, the site asks for the code from your app.
3. Check that the code on the site matches the one in the launcher and click **Allow sign-in**. The launcher greets you and opens the main window.

The code is valid for 10 minutes; while it waits, the launcher shows the time left (*Waiting for approval · 9:59*). **Open again** reopens the page, **Copy link** copies the link and the code, and **Back** returns to the choice.

The launcher remembers your sign-in and next time opens the main window at once.

### If sign-in doesn't work

| What it says | What to do |
|---|---|
| *The browser did not open. Go to the address below and enter this code.* | The link and the code are already on your clipboard. Open the address in any browser and enter the code. |
| *The code expired. Get a new one and confirm in the browser.* | Click **Get a new code**. |
| *Sign-in was declined in the browser.* | Someone clicked **Deny** on the site. If it was you, click **Get a new code**. |
| *Browser sign-in did not work: …* | After the colon comes the reason or NodeMP's answer. If the connection breaks, the launcher retries up to four times. Click **Get a new code**. If NodeMP names a support address, a **Support** button appears too. |

## Test Drive

**Continue as Test Drive** lets you in without an account. A guest name looks like `Guest-7K3MQ` and stays the same for every join from the same launcher installation.

Each server decides whether to let guests in: see the **Test Drive** mark in the list and the **Access** row in the server's card ([Join a server](/players/join/#find-a-server)). If a guest tries a server that needs an account, NodeMP refuses and the launcher offers **Sign in**.

Test Drive isn't remembered: the sign-in window comes back at the next start. To sign in later, click **Settings → Account → Sign in**. Guests can't wait in a full server's queue ([When the server is full](/players/join/#when-the-server-is-full)).

## Your account in the launcher

**Settings → Account** shows your name and roles. **Sign out** switches the launcher to Test Drive. The **On the site** block links to your account pages in the browser: **Profile**, **Security**, **Connections**, **My servers**, **Session** and **Public page**.

If the moderators warn you, the launcher says so and shows the reason under **Warnings from the moderators**. The site shows the warning on your profile while it is in force.

## Bans

A banned account can't join NodeMP servers. The launcher shows the *Account banned* window at startup, when you sign in, or when you join a server. The window shows **Reason**, **Until** (or *No end date*) and the account number; with no details, it says *No reason or end date was given.*

**Close** closes the launcher. If NodeMP names a support address, a **Contact support** button appears next to it. A ban with an end date lifts by itself when the date passes.

A ban on a single server comes from its host and doesn't affect other servers. The server tells you when you join: `You are banned from this server`, or the reason the host wrote.

---

# Join a server

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/players/join/

> Finding a server in the launcher, what it will send you, joining by address, and what happens between the click and the game.

You pick a server in the launcher, not in the game: the **NodeMP Multiplayer** button in the main menu only says so. First [install the launcher](/players/install/) and [sign in or choose Test Drive](/players/sign-in/).

## Find a server

The launcher opens on **Home**. If you've played before, you can rejoin your last server there or open **All servers**; if not, click **Browse servers**. The full list is on the **Servers** tab of the left rail and shows only servers running right now.

The list has the tabs **Public**, **Favorites** (servers you starred) and **Recent** (where you joined or tried to join).

A row shows the server's name (with a badge if it's official), the map, a **Test Drive** mark if it lets guests in, the country, players and slots (and **queue N** if there's a queue) and the mode. Click a column heading to sort by it; click again to reverse the order. A **can't connect** mark means the server isn't answering right now.

To narrow the list:

- The search box (`/`) matches names, tags, maps, cities and countries, descriptions and the names of the files a server sends.
- **Filters** opens the switches **Free slots**, **Players online** and **No account needed**, a **Download size** limit in megabytes (the **Stock** button keeps only servers without mods), a **Mods** choice (*No mods* or *With mods*) with the **Sends a mod named…** field, and **Map** and **Country**.

## Look at a server

Click a row to open the server's card on the right:

- a picture of the map and, under it, the host's links with icons and addresses (Discord, rules, website, donations, voice chat). Links open in your browser; a voice chat address is copied instead, to paste into Mumble or TeamSpeak;
- the name, description and tags;
- **Players**: how many are on the server; click the number to see who;
- **Access**: *Account required* or *Test Drive allowed*;
- **Content**: how many files the server sends and their size; click it to open the list (**It will send you**). If the server sends nothing, the row says *None*;
- **Mode** and **Location**.

The same list is on the website, [nodemp.com/servers](https://nodemp.com/servers). **Connect** on a server's page opens the launcher and starts joining that server at once.

## Join by address

If the host gave you an address, click **Direct Connect** above the list, enter `address:port` and click **Connect**. For example, `203.0.113.10:30814` or `example.com:30814`; put an IPv6 address in square brackets: `[2001:db8::1]:30814`.

If the server is on the list, the launcher joins it as usual. If not, it says *Not on the public list · connecting anyway…* and connects.

The launcher checks the server's certificate: for a listed server, against the one the server reported to NodeMP; for an unlisted one, against the certificate it remembered on the first connection. If the certificate doesn't match, the server card shows a warning in place of the play button. For an unlisted server it shows *The server's security certificate has changed* with **Continue** (remembers the new certificate and joins if the host reinstalled the server) and **Cancel**; for a listed server it shows *The server's security certificate didn't match* with **Refresh and join** ([Error messages](/reference/error-codes/)).

## Join

Select a server, press and hold **Hold to play** at the bottom of its card until it reads *Release to play*, then let go. The 0.4-second hold prevents joining by accident. Holding Enter, Space or a gamepad's A button works too. With **Settings → Launcher → Hold to play** off, the button reads **Play** and one click joins.

While you join, the button is replaced by a progress bar with the current step above it, details below it and **Cancel** (or Esc), which stops the join:

1. *Checking for a launcher update*: with automatic update checks on, the launcher installs its own update if there is one ([Launcher updates](/players/install/#launcher-updates)).
2. *Checking client mod*: the launcher checks the client mod and downloads it if needed (*Downloading client mod …%*, *Verifying client mod*).
3. *Contacting the server*: the launcher connects, and the server lets you in or says why not.
4. *Checking your game files* (on a strict server, *Checking your game files against the server's reference*): the server decides how closely ([below](#what-the-server-checks)). A strict server first sends its reference manifest (*Fetching the server's reference manifest*), which the launcher downloads once and keeps.
5. *Downloading …* and *Installing …*: the launcher downloads the server's mods you don't have yet and installs them, showing the file number, downloaded megabytes and download speed below the bar. If a mod zip is already placed in the mods cache folder by hand and matches the server's file byte for byte by SHA-256, the launcher adds the hash suffix to its name and uses it without downloading.
6. *Starting BeamNG.drive*, then *Loading BeamNG.drive*: the game starts, the longest step. If the Steam copy of the game is already running, the launcher uses it instead of starting a second one.
7. *Entering the world*: the map loads and you appear on the server.

When the game starts, the launcher hides in an icon in the Windows notification area; click the icon to bring it back. It also comes back by itself when you close BeamNG.drive or when the session ends against your will: a kick, or a connection that didn't recover. With **Close the launcher once the game starts** on, the launcher closes instead.

If the join fails, a notification says why ([What the launcher says](/players/troubleshooting/#what-the-launcher-says)).

### When the server is full

If a full server has a queue, a signed-in player waits in it. The join line shows your place (*In queue: 3 of 7*) and what the launcher does meanwhile: it checks your game files and downloads mods, so the game starts as soon as your turn comes. If the host paused the queue, their note shows under your place. **Cancel** leaves the queue. A guest, or anyone on a server without a queue, gets `Server full!`. How the queue works: [The join queue](/hosting/join-queue/).

## What the server checks

Before you join, the launcher checks the game files on your computer and sends the server only the result. The server decides how strict the check is:

- A normal server has the launcher compare the game files with the game's own file list, leaving your user folder and mods alone. If it refuses you, verify the game files in Steam.
- A strict server has the launcher compare your installation and user folder with a clean installation the host prepared. If it refuses you, see [A strict server refuses you](/players/troubleshooting/#a-strict-server-refuses-you). How the check works is on the [page for hosts](/hosting/strict-verification/).

Your zip mods in `mods\` don't break the check, but the client mod deactivates them for the session unless the server permits client mods (`[server] allow_client_mods = true`), and always deactivates them in a strict session.

---

# In the game

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/players/in-game/

> The session panel and the player list, the chat, NodeMP's keys, and how to leave a server.

NodeMP's interface in the game is the session panel and the chat. Their labels are in English unless BeamNG.drive is set to Russian.

## The session panel

The panel in a corner of the screen shows the server's name, your ping (*24 ms*) and the number of players (*7/16 players*). Move it in the game's UI layout editor.

Click the player count or press `Tab` to open the list with each player's ping. A player who lost connection is marked with an icon; on your screen, their cars are stopped and see-through.

Click another player's row for **Spectate** (you ride in their car as a passenger) and **Teleport camera** (the free camera moves 7 meters behind their car and 3 meters above it). Neither works in a strict session ([Settings](/players/settings/#the-nodemp-tab-in-the-game)).

A lime tab with a number to the left of the panel counts other players' cars waiting for you to accept them. Click it to build them at once ([Other players' new cars and changes](/players/settings/#other-players-new-cars-and-changes)).

## Chat

`T` opens the chat; Enter sends a line and keeps the chat open. Esc, or Enter on an empty line, closes it. The up and down arrows bring back earlier lines, and typing `@` opens player mention suggestions that `Tab` autocompletes. While the chat is open, your car ignores the keyboard.

A line you send is pale at first, marked *sending…*, and turns normal when the server confirms it. With no confirmation within five seconds, you see *Not delivered: the server did not answer.* If the server refuses the line, the reason replaces it: you write too often, you are muted, the filter caught it, or a server plugin rejected it. A line longer than the server allows isn't sent; the mod writes *Not sent: the message is too long.*

Lines starting with `/` are commands for the server's plugins; the host knows which exist. A command no plugin takes shows for everyone as an ordinary line. Color text with codes such as `^1` and `^#RRGGBB` (all codes: [Chat and commands](/plugins/chat/)).

Set how the chat looks in the **Chat** section of the NodeMP tab ([Settings](/players/settings/#the-nodemp-tab-in-the-game)).

## Keys

Change the keys in the game's controls settings, where NodeMP's actions start with *NodeMP:*.

| Default | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `T` | NodeMP: Chat | Opens the chat. |
| `Tab` | NodeMP: Player list | Shows or hides the player list. |
| not bound | NodeMP: Settings | Opens the NodeMP tab. |
| not bound | NodeMP: Load scheduled changes | Builds all waiting cars of other players at once. |
| not bound | NodeMP: Diagnostics window | Opens the diagnostics window. |
| not bound | NodeMP: Toggle debug chat | Shows or hides the overlay window with the chat. |
| not bound | NodeMP: Join grabbed node (alias) | Repeats the game's own node grabber action (middle mouse by default): while you hold a node, links it to the node under the cursor or pins it to the world. |

## Leave

Press and hold **Leave** on the session panel until the button fills, then let go. The game returns to the main menu, but the launcher window doesn't come back by itself: click the NodeMP icon in the Windows notification area. You can't switch servers from inside the game; pick one in the launcher.

If the server ends the session, the launcher comes back with the reason ([You got dropped](/players/troubleshooting/#you-got-dropped)). If the connection drops, the launcher tries to put you back on the server ([When the connection drops](/players/connection/#when-the-connection-drops)).

---

# Settings

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/players/settings/

> The launcher's settings, the NodeMP tab in the game's settings, the Content tab with downloaded mods, and what the locked rows mean.

Settings are in two places. The launcher has what you need before the game starts. The **NodeMP** tab in the game's own settings has what you see during a session and how other players' cars behave. Changes apply at once unless the row says otherwise.

## In the launcher

The gear at the bottom of the left rail opens **Settings** with the pages **Game**, **Launcher** and **Account**.

**Game**

- **Where BeamNG.drive is installed**: the path to the game, with the **Browse** and **Find it** buttons ([The launcher can't find the game](/players/install/#the-launcher-cant-find-the-game)).
- **Graphics mode**: *Direct3D 12* (the default in BeamNG 0.40), *Vulkan* or *Direct3D 11*, the fallback if D3D12 doesn't work. The game starts in the chosen mode without asking.
- **Client mod**: the installed version and the **Check now** button ([The client mod](/players/install/#the-client-mod)).

**Launcher**

- **Language**: *Русский* or *English*. On the first start the launcher follows the system: Russian on a Russian Windows, English otherwise. Texts from servers and the game stay as they were written.
- **Hold to play**: when off, one click joins ([Join](/players/join/#join)).
- **Start with Windows**.
- **Close the launcher once the game starts**: off by default, so the launcher hides in the notification area instead ([Join](/players/join/#join)).
- **Updates**: the launcher's version, the check, automatic checks, background downloads, the channel and going back to the previous version ([Launcher updates](/players/install/#launcher-updates)).
- **Folders**: **Mods folder** (click the path to open it, **Browse** to choose another folder, or **Default** to reset it) and **Logs** with **Open**.
- **Reset**: returns the launcher's settings to their defaults. The **Favorites** and **Recent** lists and downloaded mods stay.

**Account**: your name, links to your profile, **Sign in** or **Sign out** ([Your account in the launcher](/players/sign-in/#your-account-in-the-launcher)).

### Downloaded mods

The **Content** tab on the left rail lists every file servers have sent you, with its size and download date. The search box filters by name, **Open folder** opens the cache, and **Re-read the cache folder** refreshes the list after you change files by hand.

To free space, click **Remove**: the launcher shows how much it frees and asks you to confirm. Close BeamNG.drive first: the game holds the file while it runs. If you need the mod again, the server sends it on your next join.

## The NodeMP tab in the game

BeamNG.drive's settings get a **NodeMP** tab. The **NodeMP settings** button on the pause menu's mods tab also opens it, as does a key bound to *NodeMP: Settings*. The tab has a search box, and **Show advanced settings** reveals the rarer rows: overlay colors, the synced node grabber, and the launcher's port and address.

A row can be locked. *Set by the server* means the server decides it for everyone for the session. *Locked by the strict session* means a server plugin put you in a strict session. In one, you can't use the free camera without the server's permission, **Spectate** and **Teleport camera** don't work, you can't get into cars the server didn't seat you in or open the console or the editor, and local mods are off. How plugins turn it on: [Client scripts](/plugins/client-scripting/#strict-sessions). When you leave the server, your own values come back.

Each row's hint on the tab says what it does. The sections:

| Section | What's in it |
|---|---|
| **Players** | Name tags over cars, markers for cars and for players in free camera, the face and color of your walking character (also used for your occupant in cars), player IDs. |
| **Chat** | How many lines show while the chat is closed and for how long, timestamps, words hidden as `***` on your screen only, the overlay window with the chat and the player list. |
| **Cars & network** | **My cars**: sending edits (at most once every 15 seconds), protecting your configs from cloning, **Access to my cars**, triggers and grabbing with Ctrl. **Other players' cars**: when their new cars and changes are built ([below](#other-players-new-cars-and-changes)), **Ghost cars after a reset** (for 1.5 seconds after a reset, another player's car doesn't collide with yours), simplified models. |
| **Debug** | **Full debug mode (all diagnostics)**, launcher packet logs, detailed sync logs, position-sync diagnostics, state-sync breadcrumbs, and the **Diagnostics window (ImGui)** button. |

### Other players' new cars and changes

When another player spawns a car or changes its parts, tuning or model, BeamNG.drive rebuilds that car on your computer and freezes meanwhile. The client mod holds such changes and applies them at a better moment, so the game doesn't freeze mid-corner. The [session panel](/players/in-game/#the-session-panel) shows how many cars are waiting.

How long cars wait is set in **Cars & network → Other players' cars**:

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| **Schedule other players' car changes** | On. When off, every change is built as soon as it arrives. |
| **Auto-apply other players' events** | On. When off, scheduled cars and changes are built only by hand with the button on the session panel or a key. |
| **Apply scheduled changes**: *At 0 km/h after N s (resets if km/h > 0)*, *When I stop, at least every N s*, *Every N s*, *Only when I stop*, or *Only with the button* | *At 0 km/h after N s (resets if km/h > 0)* |
| **N: wait time at 0 km/h (stop)** | 3 seconds. In the 0 km/h mode, the countdown resets if your car's speed goes above 0 km/h. On foot or without a car also counts as stopped. |
| **N: longest wait** | 30 seconds, counted from the first change that arrived (for *When I stop, at least every N s* and *Every N s*). |
| **Stopped: slower than** | 0 km/h (for *When I stop, at least every N s* and *Only when I stop*). |

Some changes apply at once: deletions, resets, color changes, people on foot, and the car you sit in, even as a passenger. A server can turn waiting off for everyone (a race, a league) or require everything to be built within a set time. Then the row says *Set by the server*, and **Applied by the server within** shows that time. How a host sets this up: [Configuring the server](/hosting/server-toml/).

---

# A bad connection and VPNs

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/players/connection/

> How to play through a VPN or on an unstable connection, what happens when the link drops, and what to do about lag and jumping cars.

## Playing through a VPN

- Don't turn the VPN on or off while you are on a server: your address changes and the launcher has to reconnect.
- Split tunneling is fine: part of the traffic may go through the tunnel and part around it. The server recognizes your packets by a session key, not by your address.
- Splitting the first packet of a connection (such as "TLS fragment" in some VPN apps) is fine too: the server waits for the whole start of the TLS connection, up to 20 seconds by default.
- A slow VPN is fine: the server stops a mod download only if it stands still for a whole minute.

## When the connection drops

A short drop doesn't kick you off the server:

1. If the server hears nothing from you for 8 seconds, your car stops and turns see-through for others, and your name gets a *LAG* mark. For the first 10 seconds of silence the driver's seat stays yours; after that another player can take it.
2. The launcher reconnects by itself. In the game you see *Connection lost, reconnecting… (N s)* and *Attempt N*.
3. If the connection returns within 30 seconds, the game goes on with the same name and cars.

If the connection doesn't return, the server closes the session and you can join again. The host can lengthen those 30 seconds, but not beyond 600: the launcher won't wait longer.

If a mod download broke off, join again: completed mods stay in the launcher's cache, and an interrupted `.part` download resumes from the byte where it stopped on the next try.

## Lag and jumping cars

Each player's own game simulates their car and sends its position 60 times a second. When packets arrive late or in bursts, your game pulls the other car to its real position, and the car jumps or slides sideways. If only one player's car jumps, the cause is their connection, not yours: the player list on the session panel shows everyone's ping.

What helps on your side:

- Choose a server closer to you (the **Country** filter in the server list).
- Play over a cable rather than Wi-Fi, and pause big downloads and streams.
- If the game freezes when someone spawns or changes a car, check that **Schedule other players' car changes** is on ([Other players' new cars and changes](/players/settings/#other-players-new-cars-and-changes)).

## Connection error messages

`TLS handshake failed: unexpected eof while reading` when you join means the server closed the connection before the TLS handshake finished. That happens when more players join from your address at once than the host allows (through a VPN, many players share one address), or when a VPN distorts or delays the handshake. Try again in a minute. If that doesn't help, tell the host ([When the server misbehaves](/hosting/troubleshooting/#players-are-refused-at-the-door)).

Other messages: [When something breaks](/players/troubleshooting/) and [Error messages](/reference/error-codes/).

---

# When something breaks

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/players/troubleshooting/

> A server won't let you in, a strict server rejects your files, mods don't download, the game won't start or you get dropped. The usual causes and what to do.

## What the launcher says

If a join fails, the launcher shows a notification whose title names the stage: *Could not join* (before the game starts, because of the client mod or NodeMP's answer), *Could not connect* (the server didn't answer), *The server refused the join* (the server said no) or *Session ended* (the session ran, then ended). The line under the title is the reason. Servers write their reasons in English, and a host may write a ban or kick reason in any language: search for them exactly as they appear.

What each reason means and what to do: [Error messages](/reference/error-codes/).

## A strict server refuses you

A strict server lets you in only with a clean installation of the game and a clean user folder ([What the server checks](/players/join/#what-the-server-checks)). If something differs, the server's card shows a block: a heading such as `Your game files do not match this server's reference (3 problems)`, the first problem, advice after **What to do**, and a command that lists every problem, with a **Copy** button.

Things you didn't change on purpose can get in the way too:

- Leftovers of unpacked mods in the user folder: files like `info_*.json` or `*.jbeam` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BeamNG\BeamNG.drive\current\vehicles\` from mods removed long ago. Your saved configurations (`<name>.pc` with pictures) don't get in the way.
- Your own maps and scripts in the `levels\`, `lua\`, `ui\`, `art\`, `scripts\` and `gameplay\` folders inside `current\`. Move them elsewhere while you play on strict servers.
- Extra files in the game folder: third-party programs, ReShade, a mod unpacked into the game folder by mistake.
- A different game version: the game updated recently and the host's copy hasn't, or vice versa. Then the list shows files of the game itself, such as `/Bin64/BeamNG.drive.x64.exe (hash)`.

To see all the problems:

1. Close BeamNG.drive.
2. Click **Copy** next to the command.
3. Paste it into Command Prompt or PowerShell and press Enter. If the path to `NodeMP.exe` is in quotes (it is when the path has spaces), put `& ` in front of the command in PowerShell.

Each line of the result is a path and a reason:

| Reason | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `overlay` | A file in the user folder replaces or adds game content. | Remove it from `current\`. Put zip mods in `mods\`. |
| `unlisted` | An extra file in the game folder. | Delete it yourself: Steam's check doesn't remove extra files. |
| `hash`, `size`, `missing` | A game file was changed or is missing. If there are many and `/Bin64/…` is among them, you and the server have different game versions. | Verify the files in Steam, update the game, or wait for the host to update. |
| `crc`, `extra`, `duplicate` | Something is wrong inside a game archive. | Verify the files in Steam. |
| `unreadable` | The launcher couldn't read a game archive or a folder in the user folder. | If the path starts with `userfolder:`, shorten it or delete that folder. If it's a game archive, verify the files in Steam. |

During the session the launcher checks again when the server asks (every 10 minutes by default) and when files change. If something changed, the server ends the session: put the files back and join again. How the check works and how a host sets it up: [Strict file check](/hosting/strict-verification/).

## Mods don't download

- The download is slow: wait. As long as it moves, the server doesn't cut it off.
- The download broke off: see [A bad connection and VPNs](/players/connection/#when-the-connection-drops).
- The same mod fails every time: the server may not have it, the file may be broken, or the host marked it as protected and you have to put it in the cache yourself; the message then names the folder. All such messages: [Downloading the server's mods](/reference/error-codes/#downloading-the-servers-mods).
- The disk is full: delete mods you don't need on the **Content** tab ([Downloaded mods](/players/settings/#downloaded-mods)).

## The game doesn't start, or closes right away

1. Open **Settings → Game** and check that the launcher sees the game version. If it doesn't, click **Browse** or **Find it** ([The launcher can't find the game](/players/install/#the-launcher-cant-find-the-game)).
2. Choose another **Graphics mode** there, such as *Direct3D 11*.
3. Verify the game files in Steam.
4. If the game started and closed, look for the reason in its log, `beamng.log` ([where it is](#what-to-send-when-you-ask-for-help)).

If the game started but showed the error `Error loading NodeMP` with the text `NodeMP is not compatible with BeamNG.drive version …`, your game isn't from the 0.40 branch the mod is built for ([What you need](/players/install/#what-you-need)).

## You got dropped

A short drop doesn't end the session ([When the connection drops](/players/connection/#when-the-connection-drops)). If the session did end, the launcher comes back and names the reason in a *Session ended* notification; what it means is under [The server's refusals and kicks](/reference/error-codes/#the-servers-refusals-and-kicks).

## The server list is empty

- *Connection lost* at startup: [The first start](/players/install/#the-first-start).
- *No servers online*: the list loaded, but no server is running right now.
- *Nothing matches these filters*: there are servers, but your filters hide them. Click **Reset all filters**.
- A server you know is running isn't on the list: the host may not have listed it. Join [by address](/players/join/#join-by-address).

## The launcher's traffic helper

For every join, the launcher starts a second copy of itself without a window. It starts the game, connects to the server and carries your traffic while you play. *The launcher's traffic helper stopped* refers to this background part, and the line under the title is the last line of its log. What it means: [Helper exit codes](/reference/error-codes/#helper-exit-codes).

## What to send when you ask for help

On Discord, send:

1. `launcher.log` right after the problem: the launcher starts it over on the next join.
2. The exact text of the message: the title, the line under it and the text from **Details**.
3. The server's name and what you were doing.

If the problem is inside the game (a car disappeared, the chat acts strangely), add the game's log, `beamng.log`.

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| `launcher.log` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NodeMP\helper\logs\` (**Settings → Launcher → Folders → Logs → Open**) |
| `beamng.log` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BeamNG\BeamNG.drive\current\` |
| Mods downloaded from servers | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NodeMP\helper\cache\` (**Settings → Launcher → Folders → Downloaded content → Open**) |
| The client mod | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BeamNG\BeamNG.drive\current\mods\multiplayer\NodeMP.zip` |
| Remembered server certificates (delete a server's line if the host reinstalled it) | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NodeMP\helper\cache\known_servers.json` |
| `Launcher.cfg`, the helper's settings | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NodeMP\helper\`. You don't need to edit it: the launcher passes everything a join needs. |

The table gives the game's default user folder; if you moved it, the paths start from yours.

---

# Run a server

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/hosting/quick-start/

> What a NodeMP server needs, where to get Node-Server, and how to get from the download to your first join.

`Node-Server` is the program players connect to. It runs on Windows, on Linux and in Docker. You don't need an account to run one: without one, the server isn't in the public list, and players join by address.

## What you need

- A computer or a VPS that players can reach on one port, over TCP and UDP. The default is `30814`. If the server is at home, forward the port on your router.
- Windows x64 or Linux x64 ([what Linux needs](/hosting/linux/)).
- An account at [nodemp.com](https://nodemp.com), if the server should be in the list.

## Steps

1. Download and start the server. The Windows and Linux archives are on the [download page](https://nodemp.com/download) in the **Your own server** block, with their checksums. Instructions for each system: [Windows](/hosting/windows/), [Linux](/hosting/linux/) or [Docker](/hosting/docker/).
2. Open port `30814` for TCP and UDP. The firewall commands are on the same pages.
3. Set the name, the map and the number of slots ([below](#name-map-and-slots)).
4. Add the server to the list with a server key: [Get listed](/hosting/registering/).
5. Join it from the launcher ([below](#join-your-server)).

The same files are on [GitHub](https://github.com/NodeMP-BeamNG/releases/releases) under the tag `server-v<version>`: the Windows archive, the Linux archive and a `.sha256` file next to each.

## The first start

On its first start the server writes a short `server.toml` with the settings a host usually changes, creates a TLS certificate and the `content/` and `logs/` folders. When all is well, the console shows:

```text
listening on [::]:30814 (udp, dual-stack: IPv4 + IPv6)
listening on [::]:30814 (tcp, tls 1.3, dual-stack: IPv4 + IPv6)
server is ready
```

To stop the server, press Ctrl+C or type `stop` in its window.

## Name, map and slots

Open `server.toml` and change the lines in the `[server]` table:

```toml
[server]
name = "Evening freeroam"
map = "/levels/west_coast_usa/info.json"
max_players = 16
cars_per_player = 2
```

The map is the path to its `info.json`: `/levels/<map folder>/info.json`. To use a map of your own, see [Mods and maps](/hosting/mods/). `max_players` is how many players the server takes, and `cars_per_player` how many cars each of them can have.

Save the file and restart the server. The other settings are in [Configuring the server](/hosting/server-toml/) and [Settings reference](/hosting/configuration/). In Docker there is no file; the same settings are environment variables ([Server in Docker](/hosting/docker/)).

## Join your server

A server with a key shows up in the **Servers** tab of the launcher. A server without a key isn't in the list: click **Direct Connect** and enter its public address with the port, such as `203.0.113.10:30814` ([Join a server](/players/join/#join-by-address)). From a computer on the same home network, use the server's local address, such as `192.168.1.20:30814`.

---

# Server on Windows

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/hosting/windows/

> Download Node-Server for Windows, check the archive, start it, open the port in the firewall and start the server with Windows.

## Download

On the [download page](https://nodemp.com/download), in the **Your own server** block, click **Windows x64**. The checksum is in the same block, under **Checksums and Docker**. On [GitHub](https://github.com/NodeMP-BeamNG/releases/releases) the release has two files for Windows: `Node-Server-<version>-windows-x64.zip` and `Node-Server-<version>-windows-x64.zip.sha256`.

To check that the archive downloaded intact, run this in PowerShell in your Downloads folder:

```powershell
$zip = "Node-Server-<version>-windows-x64.zip"
(Get-FileHash $zip).Hash.ToLower()
(Get-Content "$zip.sha256").Split(" ")[0]
```

The two lines must match. If they don't, download the archive again.

## Unpack and start

Unpack the archive into a folder of its own, such as `C:\NodeMP`, and double-click `Node-Server.exe`. Or start it from PowerShell:

```powershell
cd C:\NodeMP
.\Node-Server.exe
```

The server's window is also its console: it shows the log and the chat, and you type commands there ([Console, kicks and bans](/hosting/administration/)). Keep the window open while you need the server: closing it stops the server.

The folder holds:

- `Node-Server.exe`, the server;
- `tools/`, the client-script obfuscator and the Lua 5.1 it runs on, with nothing to set up;
- `modules/`, the database module for plugins;
- `examples/`, ready-made example plugins ([The example plugins](/plugins/examples/));
- `cacert.pem`, root certificates in case the system has none. Don't delete it.

## Open the port

Open PowerShell as administrator and allow incoming connections on the server's port:

```powershell
$port = 30814
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "NodeMP TCP" -Direction Inbound `
  -Protocol TCP -LocalPort $port -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "NodeMP UDP" -Direction Inbound `
  -Protocol UDP -LocalPort $port -Action Allow
```

If the computer is behind a router, forward the same port to it, TCP and UDP, and test it from outside ([The server can't be reached](/hosting/troubleshooting/#the-server-cant-be-reached)).

## Start with Windows

To have the server start by itself after a reboot, create a task in **Task Scheduler**:

1. In **Task Scheduler**, choose **Action → Create Task**.
2. On the **General** tab, choose **Run whether user is logged on or not**.
3. On the **Triggers** tab, add the trigger **At startup**.
4. On the **Actions** tab, add the action **Start a program** with `C:\NodeMP\Node-Server.exe` as the program and `C:\NodeMP` in **Start in**.

**Start in** sets the server's working directory, where it looks for `server.toml`, `resources/` and `content/`. A server started this way has no window, and so no console.

---

# Server on Linux

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/hosting/linux/

> Download Node-Server for Linux, install Lua 5.1 for the obfuscator, open the port and run the server as a systemd service.

The Linux build is for x64 and is built on Ubuntu 24.04. On an older system, run the [Docker image](/hosting/docker/).

## Download and unpack

On the [download page](https://nodemp.com/download), the **Linux x64** button in the **Your own server** block downloads the archive. On a machine without a browser, take it from GitHub:

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /opt/nodemp && sudo chown "$USER" /opt/nodemp
cd /opt/nodemp
version=<version>
url=https://github.com/NodeMP-BeamNG/releases/releases/download/server-v$version
curl -LO "$url/Node-Server-$version-linux-x64.tar.gz"
curl -LO "$url/Node-Server-$version-linux-x64.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c Node-Server-$version-linux-x64.tar.gz.sha256
tar -xzf Node-Server-$version-linux-x64.tar.gz
```

`sha256sum` must print `OK`. The folder now holds `Node-Server`, `tools/`, `modules/` and `examples/`.

## Install Lua 5.1

Before sending plugins' client scripts to players, the server obfuscates them. The obfuscator is written in Lua and runs on Lua 5.1, which the Linux archive doesn't include:

```bash
sudo apt install -y lua5.1
```

The server takes the path to it from the `NODE_LUA` variable. Without Lua the server still works; it sends the client scripts as they are and says so at start.

## Start it

```bash
NODE_LUA=/usr/bin/lua5.1 ./Node-Server
```

The server writes `server.toml`, `logs/` and `content/` into the current folder. Stop it with Ctrl+C or the `stop` command.

## Open the port

With `ufw`:

```bash
sudo ufw allow 30814/tcp
sudo ufw allow 30814/udp
```

Many VPS providers also have a firewall in their control panel: open the port there too.

## A systemd service

A service starts the server with the system and restarts it after a crash. Create a user for the server and give it the folder:

```bash
sudo useradd -r -s /usr/sbin/nologin -d /opt/nodemp nodemp
sudo chown -R nodemp:nodemp /opt/nodemp
```

Create the file `/etc/systemd/system/nodemp.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=NodeMP server
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
User=nodemp
WorkingDirectory=/opt/nodemp
Environment=NODE_LUA=/usr/bin/lua5.1
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/nodemp.env
ExecStart=/opt/nodemp/Node-Server
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Enable and start the service, then follow the log:

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nodemp
journalctl -u nodemp -f
```

Keep secrets, such as the server key, in `/etc/nodemp.env`, one `NAME=value` per line, and not in `server.toml` ([Put the key into the settings](/hosting/registering/#put-the-key-into-the-settings)).

A service has no terminal, so it has no console. Stop the server with `sudo systemctl stop nodemp`, and kick and ban players with plugins ([Console, kicks and bans](/hosting/administration/#kicks-and-bans)).

---

# Server in Docker

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/hosting/docker/

> How to get the Node-Server image, prepare a data folder, run the container with docker run or Compose and set it up with variables.

The image runs on any Linux with Docker, including systems older than the Ubuntu 24.04 it is built on. It already has Lua 5.1 for the obfuscator and a health check for the container.

## Get the image

The image is in the `ghcr.io` registry. Its tag is the release tag without `server-`: a `v` and the version number:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/nodemp-beamng/server:<tag>
```

On the [download page](https://nodemp.com/download), in the **Your own server** block under **Checksums and Docker**, this command is already filled in with the right tag. Don't use the `latest` tag: it's built from the code in development, not from a release.

## How the container works

- By default the image doesn't read `server.toml`: each setting has an environment variable of its own, `NODE_NAME` for `[server] name` and so on. The full list is in the [settings reference](/hosting/configuration/). To have the image read the file: [`server.toml` isn't read](/hosting/troubleshooting/#servertoml-isnt-read).
- The server's data is in `/data`: plugins, mods, storage, bans, logs. The server can't change the program's own folder.
- The server runs as user 10001, and the data folder must belong to it.
- The TLS certificate must be in `/data` too. By default the server puts it next to the program, which is read-only in the image. The variables below move it to `/data/tls`.

## Prepare the data folder

```bash
mkdir -p data && sudo chown 10001:10001 data
```

## Run it

```bash
docker run -d --name nodemp --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 30814:30814/tcp -p 30814:30814/udp \
  -v "$PWD/data:/data" \
  -e NODE_TLS_CERT=/data/tls/node_cert.pem \
  -e NODE_TLS_KEY=/data/tls/node_key.pem \
  -e NODE_NAME="Evening freeroam" \
  -e NODE_MAP=/levels/west_coast_usa/info.json \
  ghcr.io/nodemp-beamng/server:<tag>
```

`-p` publishes the port the server listens on, for TCP and UDP. If you change the port with `NODE_PORT`, change it in `-p` too. The image's metadata (`EXPOSE`) names port `25565`, which the server doesn't listen on, so `-P` doesn't work: publish the port explicitly.

To follow the log:

```bash
docker logs -f nodemp
```

To change a setting, remove the container (`docker rm -f nodemp`) and run it again with the new variables. The `data/` folder isn't touched.

## The same with Compose

With Compose you keep the settings in a file. Put a `compose.yaml` next to the `data/` folder:

```yaml
services:
  nodemp:
    image: ghcr.io/nodemp-beamng/server:<tag>
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["30814:30814/tcp", "30814:30814/udp"]
    volumes: ["./data:/data"]
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      NODE_TLS_CERT: /data/tls/node_cert.pem
      NODE_TLS_KEY: /data/tls/node_key.pem
      NODE_NAME: Evening freeroam
      NODE_MAP: /levels/west_coast_usa/info.json
```

Put the secrets, such as the server key ([Get listed](/hosting/registering/)), in a `.env` file next to it, readable only by you (`chmod 600 .env`). Until you have secrets the file can be empty, but it must exist (`touch .env`). Then:

```bash
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f
```

After editing `compose.yaml`, run `docker compose up -d` again: Compose recreates the container, and `data/` stays as it is.

## The console

`stdin_open` and `tty` give the server a terminal, and the server then has a console. To attach to it:

```bash
docker attach nodemp
```

If you started the container with Compose and no `container_name`, `docker compose ps` shows its name. To leave without stopping the server, press Ctrl+P, then Ctrl+Q. With `docker run`, the console appears if you add `-it`.

## Plugins and mods

Copy plugins into `data/resources/` and mods into `data/content/`. The files must be readable by user 10001, so run `sudo chown -R 10001:10001 data` after copying. The server reads mods at start, so restart the container afterward (`docker restart nodemp`).

Native modules are inside the image, not in `/data`: to add one, build your own image on top of this one.

---

# Configuring the server

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/hosting/server-toml/

> How server.toml works, the settings hosts change most, environment variables and command-line options.

The server keeps its settings in one file, `server.toml`, in its working directory. Every key, with its type and default, is in the [settings reference](/hosting/configuration/).

## How the file works

On its first start the server writes a short file with the tables a host fills in: `[server]`, `[vehicles]` and `[listing]`.

```toml
# NodeMP server settings: https://docs.nodemp.com/hosting/configuration/
# Environment variables (NODE_PORT, NODE_NAME, ...) win over this file.

[server]
name = "Node Server"
port = 30814
max_players = 8
cars_per_player = 1
map = "/levels/gridmap_v2/info.json"
mods = "content"  # folder of mod zips players download

[vehicles]
queue = "allow"  # "off": every client applies at once (races, leagues)
queue_max_delay_sec = 0  # not 0: a client must apply within N s
edit_interval_sec = 5  # edits of one car reach the others at most once per N s
spawn_interval_sec = 2  # one player's new cars at most once per N s

[listing]
url = ""  # "https://api.nodemp.com" to be listed in the launcher
host_id = ""
host_secret = ""  # or NODE_DIRECTORY_HOST_SECRET, out of this file
description = ""
mode = "freeroam"
tags = ""
preview = ""  # a JPEG or PNG; empty: the map's own
public = true
guests = true  # players without a NodeMP account
```

- A setting that isn't in the file keeps its default. To change it, write it into its table, and add the table if the file doesn't have it yet.
- The server reads the file at start, so restart it after an edit.
- The server rejects a value of the wrong type or out of range: the default stays, and the log has a warning. The server also warns about an unknown key and names it, which is how a typo shows up.
- A table or a key written twice stops the server from starting. The message names the file and the line ([The server won't start](/hosting/troubleshooting/#the-server-wont-start)).
- Lists (`connection_limit_exempt`, `masked_commands`, `trusted`) can be a comma-separated string or a TOML list.

## What people change most

### Name, map and slots

These are `name`, `map`, `max_players` and `cars_per_player` in `[server]`. An example: [Run a server](/hosting/quick-start/#name-map-and-slots).

### The port

`[server] port` (`30814` by default) sets one port for both TCP and UDP. To make the server listen on every address, IPv4 and IPv6, leave `address` at `"::"`.

### The game file check

`[integrity] verify` sets how closely the launcher checks the player's game files:

- `"off"`: the server asks for nothing, but the launcher still checks `size`.
- `"size"`: the size of every game file and extra files in the game's `content/`. The default.
- `"scripts"`: the same, plus checksums of the game's `lua/` and `ui/`. Catches edited scripts.
- `"full"`: checksums of the whole game, about 50 GB, archives included. This is an audit, too slow for a check before joining.
- `"strict"`: the same as `scripts`, plus a comparison of the archives' tables of contents, the whole game folder and the user folder with a reference of a clean install ([Strict file check](/hosting/strict-verification/)).

### A place in the server list

The `[listing]` table sets it, including the links to your server's Discord, rules, site and voice chat. How to fill it in: [Get listed](/hosting/registering/).

### Chat

Chat is built into the server. `[chat] max_length`, `rate_per_sec` and `burst` limit the length of a line and how often a player can write, so that nobody floods the chat.

### Other players' cars

The client mod holds back other players' new cars and changes so that the game doesn't freeze to rebuild them mid-corner, and each player decides when to apply them ([what players see](/players/settings/#other-players-new-cars-and-changes)). For a race or a league, where everyone must see the same cars at once, you can turn the waiting off, or require that everything is built within a set time:

```toml
[vehicles]
queue = "off"            # or: queue = "allow" and queue_max_delay_sec = 10
```

A plugin can also switch this during a session and build everything before a start ([Players and vehicles](/plugins/players-and-vehicles/)). `edit_interval_sec` and `spawn_interval_sec` cut the number of rebuilds further ([Settings reference](/hosting/configuration/#vehicles)).

### Bad connections

A player who is silent for `lag_grace_sec` seconds counts as lagging, and after `disconnect_sec` the player is disconnected ([Settings reference](/hosting/configuration/#network)). For players on mobile data or a VPN, allow more time:

```toml
[network]
disconnect_sec = 60
```

More than 600 seconds doesn't help: after 600 seconds the launcher stops trying to come back. The timers must stay in order or the server won't start: `lag_grace_sec < seat_takeover_sec <= seat_release_sec <= disconnect_sec`, and `lag_grace_sec` is at least 1.

## Environment variables

Every setting has an environment variable of its own, named in the [settings reference](/hosting/configuration/). The variable wins over the file, and `--port` on the command line wins over both. Keep secrets such as `host_secret` in the environment: then they don't end up in a file that gets copied and sent around.

A few variables aren't settings:

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `NODE_LUA` | The path to Lua 5.1 for the obfuscator. Needed on Linux. |
| `NODE_TOOLS_DIR` | Another place for the `tools/` folder. |
| `NODE_PROVIDER_DISABLE_CONFIG` | `true` or `1` stops the server from reading `server.toml` and takes everything from the environment. The Docker image works this way. |
| `NODE_PROVIDER_IP_ENV`, `NODE_PROVIDER_PORT_ENV` | For hosting panels: the name of the variable in which the panel passes the address and the port. |
| `NODE_HEARTBEAT_FILE` | A file the server keeps updating while it runs. Docker's health check reads it. |
| `NODE_FORCE_ANSI` | `1` or `true` keeps the colors even when the output isn't a terminal. |

## Command line

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--config=FILE` | Which settings file to read. By default `server.toml` in the working directory. Put a path with spaces in quotes. |
| `--port=N` | The TCP and UDP port. Wins over the file and the environment. |
| `--working-directory=DIR` | The working directory: every relative path starts there, including the path in `--config`. |
| `--version` | Print the version and exit. |
| `--help` | Print the help and exit. |
| `--gen-integrity GAMEDIR` | Make the reference manifest for the strict check ([Strict file check](/hosting/strict-verification/#make-the-manifest)). |
| `--bans list`, `--bans remove …` | Show or lift bans while the server is stopped ([Console, kicks and bans](/hosting/administration/#bans)). |
| `--obf-selftest` | Check that the obfuscator works. |

A value may also follow its option after a space: `--port 30815`. To run two servers on one machine, give each its own working directory and port:

```bash
./Node-Server --working-directory=/srv/nodemp-2 --port=30815
```

---

# Configuration reference

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/hosting/configuration/

> Every server setting by section, with environment variables, descriptions, and options.

The keys of `server.toml` in the order the server declares them. Strings are in quotes, as in the file. How the file, environment variables and command line work: [Configuring the server](/hosting/server-toml/).

## `[server]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `NODE_NAME` | The server's name in the server list and in the game. Default `"Node Server"`. |
| `port` | `NODE_PORT` | The TCP and UDP port players connect to. Default `30814`. |
| `max_players` | `NODE_MAX_PLAYERS` | How many players can be on the server at once. Default `8`. |
| `cars_per_player` | `NODE_MAX_CARS` | How many cars one player can have. Default `1`. |
| `map` | `NODE_MAP` | The map, as the path to its `info.json`. Default `"/levels/gridmap_v2/info.json"`. |
| `mods` | `NODE_CONTENT_FOLDER` | The folder with the mod zips players download. Default `"content"`. |
| `mods_url` | `NODE_MODS_URL` | Base HTTP/HTTPS URL of an external mirror or CDN serving the mod archives. Empty string serves mods directly from the server. Default `""`. |
| `allow_client_mods` | `NODE_ALLOW_CLIENT_MODS` | Allow players to load client-side mods from their client `mods` folder. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |
| `address` | `NODE_IP` | The address to listen on. `"::"` means all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. Not the server's public IP. Default `"::"`. |
| `console` | `NODE_CONSOLE` | Read console commands from standard input (for pipes and files). Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |

## `[vehicles]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `queue` | `NODE_VEHICLES_QUEUE` | Vehicle queue behavior: `"allow"` (players decide whether to hold back new cars) or `"off"` (build immediately). Default `"allow"`. |
| `queue_max_delay_sec` | `NODE_VEHICLES_QUEUE_MAX_DELAY_SEC` | Maximum queue delay in seconds (up to `3600`). `0` disables forced building. Default `0`. |
| `edit_interval_sec` | `NODE_VEHICLES_EDIT_INTERVAL_SEC` | Minimum interval in seconds between configuration updates sent to others. `0` disables the limit. Default `5`. |
| `spawn_interval_sec` | `NODE_VEHICLES_SPAWN_INTERVAL_SEC` | Minimum interval in seconds between spawning new cars by the same player. `0` disables the limit. Default `2`. |
| `delete_on_disconnect` | `NODE_VEHICLES_DELETE_ON_DISCONNECT` | Delete player's spawned vehicles after disconnect. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `true`. |
| `delete_on_disconnect_sec` | `NODE_VEHICLES_DELETE_ON_DISCONNECT_SEC` | Seconds before deleting a disconnected player's empty vehicles (`0` deletes immediately). Default `60`. |
| `delete_idle_sec` | `NODE_VEHICLES_DELETE_IDLE_SEC` | Auto-delete unoccupied vehicles after this many seconds (`0` disables idle cleanup). Default `0`. |

## `[listing]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_URL` | Directory server address: `"https://api.nodemp.com"`. Empty string leaves the server unlisted. Default `""`. |
| `host_id` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_HOST_ID` | Public identifier part of the server directory keypair. |
| `host_secret` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_HOST_SECRET` | Secret key part of the server directory keypair. Keep confidential. |
| `description` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_DESCRIPTION` | Short server description (1–2 sentences under the server name). |
| `mode` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_MODE` | Server game mode column in the list: `freeroam`, `racing`, `roleplay`, `drift`, etc. Default `"freeroam"`. |
| `tags` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_TAGS` | Comma-separated tags for filtering in the list (up to 8 tags). |
| `preview` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_PREVIEW` | Custom image URL for the server card. Empty string uses the map's preview image. |
| `public` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_PUBLIC` | Show server in the public master list. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `true`. |
| `guests` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_TEST_DRIVE` | Allow players without an account to join. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `true`. |
| `fingerprint` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_FINGERPRINT` | Certificate fingerprint for a private directory. Leave empty. |
| `ca_file` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_CA_FILE` | Path to custom CA certificate for a private directory. Leave empty. |
| `admit_when_down` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_REDEEM_FAIL_OPEN` | When directory is down: `true` admits players as guests, `false` refuses logins. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |
| `allow_http` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_ALLOW_INSECURE` | Allow insecure `http://` in `url`. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |
| `discord` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_LINK_DISCORD` | Invite link to your Discord community. |
| `rules` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_LINK_RULES` | Web link to server rules page. |
| `site` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_LINK_SITE` | Web link to official server website. |
| `donate` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_LINK_DONATE` | Web link to server support / donation page. |
| `voice` | `NODE_DIRECTORY_LINK_VOICE` | Web link to voice chat server. |

## `[integrity]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `verify` | `NODE_VERIFY_GAME` | Game file integrity check level. Options: `off`, `size`, `scripts`, `full`, `strict`. Default `"size"`. |
| `manifests` | `NODE_INTEGRITY_DIR` | Folder containing reference manifests for `strict` mode. Default `"integrity"`. |
| `recheck_sec` | `NODE_INTEGRITY_RECHECK_SEC` | Periodic recheck interval in seconds in `strict` mode. `0` disables periodic checks. Default `600`. |
| `auto_fetch` | `NODE_INTEGRITY_AUTO_FETCH` | Automatically fetch official reference manifest from backend if no local files exist in `strict` mode. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `true`. |
| `url` | `NODE_INTEGRITY_URL` | Backend URL for downloading official reference manifests. Defaults to `[listing] url` or `"https://api.nodemp.com"`. |
| `game_version` | `NODE_INTEGRITY_GAME_VERSION` | Game version of the reference manifest to download (e.g. `"0.39.4.0"`). Default is empty string (downloads latest available). |

## `[network]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `tls_cert` | `NODE_TLS_CERT` | Server TLS certificate path. Created automatically on first run. Default `"node_cert.pem"`. |
| `tls_key` | `NODE_TLS_KEY` | Private key for the server TLS certificate. Default `"node_key.pem"`. |
| `relay_radius` | `NODE_STATE_RELAY_RADIUS` | Position relay radius in meters. `0` sends positions to all players. Default `0`. |
| `lag_grace_sec` | `NODE_NETWORK_LAG_GRACE_SEC` | Silence threshold in seconds before a player is flagged as lagging. Default `8`. |
| `seat_takeover_sec` | `NODE_NETWORK_AUTH_TAKEOVER_SEC` | Seconds a silent driver holds a seat before another player can take it over. Default `10`. |
| `seat_release_sec` | `NODE_NETWORK_AUTH_RELEASE_SEC` | Seconds of silence before the server frees the driver seat. Default `30`. |
| `disconnect_sec` | `NODE_NETWORK_DISCONNECT_SEC` | Silence timeout in seconds before dropping connection. Default `30`. |
| `send_queue_budget_mb` | `NODE_NETWORK_SEND_QUEUE_BUDGET_MB` | Memory budget in MB for all outgoing queues. `0` removes the shared limit. Default `256`. |
| `max_connections_per_ip` | `NODE_NETWORK_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_IP` | Maximum concurrent connections during handshake per IP address. Default `32`. |
| `max_connections` | `NODE_NETWORK_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | Total concurrent connections during handshake across all IP addresses. Default `256`. |
| `connection_limit_exempt` | `NODE_NETWORK_CONNECTION_LIMIT_EXEMPT` | Subnets exempt from per-IP connection limits (CIDR). Default includes local subnets. |
| `handshake_timeout_sec` | `NODE_NETWORK_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_SEC` | Timeout in seconds for TLS handshake and initial login frames. Default `20`. |
| `download_stall_sec` | `NODE_NETWORK_DOWNLOAD_STALL_SEC` | Mod download stall timeout in seconds if no data is received. Default `60`. |
| `download_rate_mb` | `NODE_NETWORK_DOWNLOAD_RATE_MB` | Per-player mod download rate limit in MB/s (up to `10000`). `0` is unlimited. Default `0`. |
| `download_total_rate_mb` | `NODE_NETWORK_DOWNLOAD_TOTAL_RATE_MB` | Total mod download rate limit across all players in MB/s (up to `100000`). `0` is unlimited. Default `0`. |
| `max_concurrent_downloads` | `NODE_NETWORK_MAX_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` | Maximum concurrent mod downloads from the server (`1` to `64`). Default `4`. |

## `[queue]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `NODE_QUEUE_ENABLED` | Enable join queue when server is full. Requires directory listing. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `true`. |
| `max_waiting` | `NODE_QUEUE_MAX_WAITING` | Maximum join queue capacity (`0` to `1000`). `0` disables queue. Default `50`. |
| `max_waiting_per_ip` | `NODE_QUEUE_MAX_WAITING_PER_IP` | Maximum queued players from a single IP address (`1` to `1000`). Default `1`. |
| `downloads_while_waiting` | `NODE_QUEUE_DOWNLOADS_WHILE_WAITING` | Number of queued players downloading mods concurrently (`1` to `64`). Default `3`. |
| `max_no_shows` | `NODE_QUEUE_MAX_NO_SHOWS` | Maximum no-shows within window before temporary queue bar. `0` disables penalty. Default `3`. |
| `no_show_window_min` | `NODE_QUEUE_NO_SHOW_WINDOW_MIN` | Time window in minutes for counting queue no-shows (`1` to `10080`). Default `60`. |
| `no_show_bar_min` | `NODE_QUEUE_NO_SHOW_BAR_MIN` | Penalty duration in minutes an account is barred from queuing. Default `30`. |

## `[chat]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `max_length` | `NODE_CHAT_MAX_LENGTH` | Maximum chat message length in bytes (`16` to `2048`). Default `256`. |
| `rate_per_sec` | `NODE_CHAT_RATE_PER_SEC` | Average messages per second allowed per player (minimum `1`). Default `2`. |
| `burst` | `NODE_CHAT_BURST` | Message burst allowed before rate limiting engages (minimum `1`). Default `5`. |
| `log` | `NODE_CHAT_LOG_TO_CONSOLE` | Log chat messages to console and `server.log`. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `true`. |
| `masked_commands` | `NODE_CHAT_LOG_HIDDEN_COMMANDS` | Commands whose arguments are masked as `***` in server logs. Default includes login keywords. |

## `[logs]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `debug` | `NODE_DEBUG` | Verbose debug log for all server components. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |
| `details` | `NODE_LOG_DETAILS` | Output statistics and service messages to terminal console. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |
| `max_size_mb` | `NODE_LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB` | Rotate `server.log` when file reaches this size in MB. `0` rotates only on start. Default `50`. |
| `keep` | `NODE_LOG_KEEP` | Number of rotated log files to keep. Default `5`. |
| `date` | `NODE_LOG_DATE` | Include date before timestamp in log lines. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |
| `netstats_sec` | `NODE_NETWORK_STATS_INTERVAL_SEC` | Interval in seconds to write player `netstats` to log. `0` logs only on disconnect. Default `15`. |

## `[sync]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `NODE_SYNC_VARIANT` | Sync variant for A/B tests that pins the `hold_tight` and `steer_lead` pair for every player (`"A"`, `"B"`, `"C"`, `"D"`). Empty string leaves the player's choice. Default `""`. |
| `hold_tight` | `NODE_SYNC_HOLD_TIGHT` | Pin tight holding of other cars for every player (`"on"`, `"off"`, or `""`). Empty string leaves the player's setting. Default `""`. |
| `steer_lead` | `NODE_SYNC_STEER_LEAD` | Pin steering look-ahead of other cars for every player (`"on"`, `"off"`, or `""`). Empty string leaves the player's setting. Default `""`. |
| `verbose_trace` | `NODE_SYNC_VERBOSE_TRACE` | Pin detailed sync trace logging for every player (`"on"`, `"off"`, or `""`). Empty string leaves the player's setting. Default `""`. |
| `trace_rate` | `NODE_SYNC_TRACE_RATE` | Pin the sampling rate in Hz of the detailed sync trace log for every player (`10`, `20`, `60`, or `0`). `0` leaves the player's setting. Default `0`. |

## `[http]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `ca_file` | `NODE_HTTP_CA_FILE` | Custom root CA certificates path for plugin HTTPS requests. |
| `insecure` | `NODE_HTTP_INSECURE` | Disable TLS certificate verification in plugin HTTPS requests. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |
| `allow_private_networks` | `NODE_HTTP_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` | Allow plugin HTTP requests to access private/local network addresses. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |

## `[resources]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `obfuscate` | `NODE_OBFUSCATE` | Obfuscate client Lua scripts before sending to players. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `true`. |
| `trusted` | `NODE_RESOURCES_TRUSTED` | Trusted plugins with full system access. `"*"` trusts all. Other plugins can only access their own directory. |

## `[experimental]`

| Key | Environment | Description and options |
|---|---|---|
| `node_grab` | `NODE_EXPERIMENTAL_NODEGRAB` | Enable experimental vehicle node grabbing with server validation. Options: `true`, `false`. Default `false`. |

# Get listed

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/hosting/registering/

> How to create a server key in your NodeMP account, put it into the settings, set how the server looks in the list and find out why it isn't there.

A server without a key works the same, and you can join it by address through **Direct Connect**. But it isn't in the server list, and it doesn't check players' names.

With a key the server reports itself to NodeMP, appears in the launcher and on [nodemp.com/servers](https://nodemp.com/servers), and every player's account is checked on join.

## Create a key

You need a NodeMP account with a linked Discord. Link Discord under **Connections** in your account, or with the **Link Discord** button on the **My servers** page.

1. Sign in at [nodemp.com](https://nodemp.com) and open [**My servers**](https://nodemp.com/account/servers).
2. Enter a label that tells this server apart from your others (only you see it) and click **Create key**.
3. In the *Server key created* window the site shows the **Host ID** and the **Host secret**. The secret is shown once, so copy it right away.

Each server needs a key of its own. **My servers** shows all your keys and when each server was last online. How many keys you can create depends on your account's roles. How many you have used is shown next to the creation form.

If the site doesn't create a key, it says why: Discord isn't linked, the account already has as many keys as it may have (delete one you don't need or rotate the secret of an existing key), or the request was refused to protect the service. In the last case the site shows a decision number: quote it to support.

## Put the key into the settings

`server.toml` already has a `[listing]` table with empty `url`, `host_id` and `host_secret`. Fill them in:

```toml
[listing]
url = "https://api.nodemp.com"
host_id = "…"
host_secret = "…"
```

:::caution[One `[listing]` table]
The site shows these three lines ready to copy. Put them into the `[listing]` table that is already in the file, and don't add a second one: TOML doesn't allow the same table twice, and the server won't start.
:::

You can set the same with environment variables, for Docker or systemd:

```text
NODE_DIRECTORY_URL=https://api.nodemp.com
NODE_DIRECTORY_HOST_ID=…
NODE_DIRECTORY_HOST_SECRET=…
```

Restart the server. It needs all three values. If all three are empty, the server doesn't report itself and says nothing about it; if only some are empty, it says so in the log. Keep the secret like a password.

## What happens next

At start the server writes `announcing this server to https://api.nodemp.com` to the log, and once the key is accepted and the list shows the server, `listed in the server browser`. After that it reports regularly, usually every 15 seconds: its name, map, number of players and slots, tags, list of mods and the fingerprint of its certificate. If NodeMP is unreachable, the server keeps running and retries by itself.

NodeMP doesn't connect to the server, so nobody checks the port from outside until players arrive. If players get join tickets for your server and none of them reaches it, NodeMP marks the server *Can't connect* on the **My servers** page, the launcher marks it in the list, and the server's log has `Listed in the server browser, but players cannot connect: …` with the port you need to forward. The mark goes away as soon as a player reaches the server. So open and forward the port for TCP and UDP, and test it from outside your own network.

While the server is listed, every join is checked: the player's launcher brings a one-time ticket, the server checks it with NodeMP and gets the account name. A player in Test Drive gets a guest name. A server without a key checks nothing and takes the name the launcher sent.

## How the server looks in the list

The other `[listing]` keys set the server's card and whom it lets in ([Settings reference](/hosting/configuration/#listing)):

```toml
[listing]
description = "Freeroam on West Coast, no ramming"
mode = "freeroam"
tags = "freeroam, no-crash, ru"
guests = true
```

- `description`: one or two sentences under the name.
- `mode`: one word, its own column in the list: `freeroam`, `racing`, `roleplay`…
- `tags`: up to eight tags, each up to 24 characters (see the [tags table](#server-tags-tags)). Players filter the list by them.
- With `guests = false` the server doesn't let in players without an account, and its card shows *Account required* in the **Access** row.
- With `public = false` the server isn't in the public list, but you can still join it by address.
- `admit_when_down` decides what happens when NodeMP can't be reached at the moment of a join: `false` (the default) refuses the player, `true` lets them in as an unverified guest.

`fingerprint`, `ca_file` and `allow_http` are only for a server list you run yourself. Leave them out for `api.nodemp.com`.

### Server tags (`tags`)

The launcher displays tags as pills on the server card and indexes them in the search filter (`/`). Players can click on a tag or type it into search to filter servers.

**Formatting rules:**
- Up to **8 tags**, separated by commas.
- Write tags in lowercase Latin letters without `#` symbols (for example: `"freeroam, drift, no-crash, eu"`).
- Use standard keywords so players can discover your server.

| Category | Common tags | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Game mode** | `freeroam`, `drift`, `racing`, `drag`, `rally`, `derby`, `chase`, `police`, `rp` | Primary gameplay: open cruise, drifting, track races, pursuits, or roleplay. |
| **Rules & Style** | `no-crash`, `crash`, `realism`, `strict`, `chill`, `chaos`, `clean-racing` | Road behavior expectations: peaceful driving without ramming, realistic driving rules, or pure chaos. |
| **Language & Region** | `en`, `ru`, `eu`, `us`, `cis`, `asia` | Primary chat language and server location for finding lowest latency. |
| **Content & Traffic** | `vanilla`, `mods`, `custom-map`, `traffic`, `bots` | Mod-free vanilla content, custom mods/maps required, or AI traffic enabled. |

**Useful examples:**
- Drift server with mods: `tags = "drift, touge, mods, ru"`
- Peaceful freeroam with traffic: `tags = "freeroam, traffic, no-crash, chill, en"`
- Racing and demolition derby: `tags = "racing, derby, crash, eu"`

### Links

In the server's details, under the map, the launcher and [nodemp.com/servers](https://nodemp.com/servers) show buttons to the server's own pages, each labeled with its domain. The `[listing]` keys set the links:

```toml
[listing]
discord = "https://discord.gg/abc123"
rules = "https://example.com/rules"
site = "https://example.com"
donate = "https://example.com/donate"
voice = "mumble://voice.example.com:64738"
```

- A link starts with `https://`. `voice` can also be `mumble://` or `ts3server://`: such an address is copied rather than opened, because only a voice chat program can open it.
- `discord` must be an invite: `https://discord.gg/…` or `https://discord.com/invite/…`.
- A link is at most 256 characters long, with no spaces and no `user:password@`.
- A link that breaks these rules isn't passed to the list at start, and the server warns, naming the key: `[listing] discord = "…" is not a link the server list shows: …; left out`.

### The picture

The server's card shows a picture of the map. It comes from:

1. `preview`, if it is set: your own JPEG or PNG of up to 2 MB. A relative path starts at the working directory. If the file can't be read, is too big or isn't an image, the server warns in the log: `No map preview is sent to the directory: …`.
2. Otherwise, for your own map from `content/`, the map's own picture from its archive.
3. For a stock map NodeMP shows the picture from the game, and the server sends nothing.

## The server's fingerprint
