```lua
    local who = node.players.find(name)
    if not who then
        player:tell("Nobody called %s here", name)
        return { handled = true }
    end
    if reason == "" then reason = "No reason given" end
    if cmd == "kick" then
        who:kick(reason)
    else
        who:ban(reason, os.time() + 24 * 3600)
    end
    node.chat.say("%s: %s (%s)", cmd, who.name, reason)
    return { handled = true }
end

node.on("chatMessageRequest", moderate)

-- expect-log: Bob kicked — flooding
```

Grant rights by `accountId`: NodeMP vouches for an account, while a guest can take any name. On a server not in the list, NodeMP verifies nobody and no one has an `accountId` ([Players and vehicles](/plugins/players-and-vehicles/#who-a-player-is)).

---

# Timers and coroutines

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/concurrency/

> Timers, coroutines that wait without blocking the server, heavy work on background threads, the 250 ms rule and a restart with a countdown in chat.

The handlers, timers and coroutines of every plugin run on one worker thread, one at a time. There are no races and no locks to take, but a long handler holds up every other plugin.

If one run holds the thread longer than 250 ms, the server logs:

```text
plugin worker job stalled the thread …
```

Wait with timers and coroutines, and hand heavy work to background threads.

## Timers

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node.after(ms, fn)` | Runs `fn` once, after `ms` milliseconds. |
| `node.every(ms, fn)` | Runs `fn` every `ms` milliseconds. A slow run delays the next; runs don't pile up. |
| `node.every(ms, fn, { precise = true })` | Keeps the schedule: missed runs follow back to back, and `fn(missed)` says how many were missed. |
| `node.cancel(id)` | Stops a timer; safe to call for one that has already fired. |
| `node.defer(fn)` | Runs `fn` as soon as the current event has been handled. |

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local ticks = 0
local id

local function countTick()
    ticks = ticks + 1
    if ticks == 3 then
        node.cancel(id)
        node.log("stopped after %d ticks", ticks)
    end
end

id = node.every(500, countTick)

-- expect: stopped after 3 ticks
```

Use `precise` when the count of runs matters: a point per second, a countdown. Ten seconds of `every(100, fn, { precise = true })` give a hundred runs even if another handler held the thread. After a long delay the timer catches up at most `maxBacklog` runs (a key of the same table, 10 by default, at most 1000); the rest are skipped, the schedule restarts from now, and the log says so once.

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local seconds = 0

local function countTime(missed)
    seconds = seconds + 0.1
    if missed > 0 then node.log("caught up %d runs", missed) end
end

node.every(100, countTime, { precise = true })

local function reportTime()
    node.log("counted %.1f s", seconds)
end

node.after(1050, reportTime)

-- expect: counted 1\.0 s
```

`serverTick` arrives on every server tick. It shares the thread with everything else, so keep it short; a timer is usually the better fit.

## Coroutines

A coroutine is code that can pause without holding the thread. `node.async(fn, ...)` starts one, and inside it `node.sleep(ms)` waits while everything else keeps running. A countdown reads top to bottom:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function countdown()
    for i = 3, 1, -1 do
        node.log("%d", i)
        node.sleep(500)
    end
    node.log("go")
end

node.async(countdown)

-- expect: ^go$
```

`node.wait(fn)` waits until `fn` returns a true value. The server calls `fn` every 50 ms; a second argument sets another interval:

<!-- doctest: server+client -->
```lua
local function somebodyIsHere()
    return node.players.count() > 0
end

local function announce()
    node.wait(somebodyIsHere)
    node.log("someone is here")
end

node.async(announce)

-- expect: someone is here
```

`node.sleep`, `node.wait`, `node.await`, `node.yield`, `node.suspend` and `node.http.fetch` work only inside `node.async`. A long loop on the worker thread gives others one turn with `node.yield()`.

`node.suspend(arm)` calls `arm(resume)` and pauses the coroutine until someone calls `resume(...)`, then returns what was passed to `resume`. It is the general form of `node.sleep` and `node.await` and turns a callback into linear code, as in `db.lua` ([The db module](/plugins/database/)).

## Heavy work

Long computations don't belong on the worker thread. `node.await(fn, args)` runs `fn` on a background thread and keeps the coroutine paused until `fn` finishes:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function sumTo(n)
    local total = 0
    for i = 1, n do
        total = total + i
    end
    return total
end

local function report()
    local sum, err = node.await(sumTo, 1000)
    node.log("sum = %s", tostring(sum or err))
end

node.async(report)

-- expect: sum = 500500
```

The background function is copied into another Lua state, so it must stand alone: no outside variables, no `node`, only its argument and plain Lua. The argument and the result travel as JSON. `node.job(fn, args, done)` does the same with a `done(result, err)` callback instead of a coroutine.

## A restart with a countdown

`node.server.shutdown(reason, delayMs)` schedules a stop, by default with the reason `Server shutdown`. `serverShutdownScheduled` tells every plugin when, so one of them can count down in chat. With `Restart=always` in systemd or a Docker restart policy, the stop becomes a restart.

<!-- doctest: server+client {"config": {"moderators": [42]}, "emit": [["chat:send", {"text": "/restart"}]]} -->
```lua
local moderators = {}
for _, id in ipairs(node.config.moderators or {}) do
    moderators[id] = true
end

local current

local function countDown(info)
    while current == info do
        local left = math.floor(info.at - node.server.unixTime())
        if left <= 0 then break end
        node.chat.say("Restart in %d s: %s", left, info.reason)
        node.sleep(math.min(left, 60) * 1000)
    end
end

local function trackShutdown(info)
    current = info
    if info.cancelled then
        node.chat.say("The restart is called off")
        return
    end
    node.async(countDown, info)
end

node.on("serverShutdownScheduled", trackShutdown)

local function handleRestart(player, msg)
    if msg.text ~= "/restart" then return end
    if moderators[player.accountId] then
        node.server.shutdown("Scheduled restart", 5 * 60 * 1000)
    end
    return { handled = true }
end

node.on("chatMessageRequest", handleRestart)

-- expect-client: Alice chat:msg .*Restart in \d+ s: Scheduled restart
```

Calling `shutdown` again replaces the schedule; a negative delay cancels it. A stop without a delay doesn't fire `serverShutdownScheduled`. When the time comes, players are disconnected with the reason, `serverShutdown` and `resourceUnload` run, and the server exits with code 0.

---

# Storage and files

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/storage/

> Keeping data with node.storage, files in the plugin's folder, safe writes, watching a file, and when a database fits better.

Lua variables are lost when a plugin reloads or the server restarts. Put what must survive in `node.storage`, in files or in a [database](/plugins/database/).

## node.storage

Each plugin has its own key-value store in `storage/` under the server's working folder: `<plugin name>.json` holds the data, `<plugin name>.log` the changes since. Values are stored as JSON: numbers, strings, booleans and tables. Each `set` is on disk before it returns, so a server crash doesn't lose it; a power cut can.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node.storage.get(key, default)` | The stored value, or `default` if there is none. |
| `node.storage.set(key, value)` | Stores the value; `false` for an unusable key or a failed write. |
| `node.storage.delete(key)` | Removes the key; `false` if it doesn't exist. |

A key is a non-empty string of up to 256 bytes. You choose the keys; a prefix keeps them apart: `visits:42`, `settings`.

A visit counter keyed by account doesn't depend on the player's name or address:

<!-- doctest: server+client -->
```lua
local function countVisit(player)
    if not player.accountId then return end
    local key = "visits:" .. player.accountId
    local visits = node.storage.get(key, 0) + 1
    node.storage.set(key, visits)
    player:tell("Visit number %d", visits)
end

node.on("playerJoined", countVisit)

-- expect-client: Alice chat:msg .*Visit number \d+
```

A table is stored and returned whole:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
node.storage.set("race", { laps = 3, track = "west" })

local race = node.storage.get("race")
node.log("laps=%d track=%s", race.laps, race.track)

-- expect: laps=3 track=west
```

The whole store is held in memory and looked up only by key: fine for settings, counters and per-player records. Data to search, sort or share between servers belongs in a database.

## Files in the plugin's folder

`node.fs` reads and writes files in the plugin's own folder. Paths count from that folder, with forward slashes; the server refuses absolute paths and `..` steps.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node.fs.read(path)` | The file's contents, or `nil`. |
| `node.fs.write(path, data)` | Writes the file, creating folders along the path. |
| `node.fs.list(path)` | The folder's entries, with `name`, `dir` and `size`. |
| `node.fs.exists(path)` | `"file"`, `"dir"` or `nil`. |
| `node.fs.stat(path)` | `{ dir, size, mtime }`, or `nil` and the reason `"outside"` or `"not found"`. |
| `node.fs.mkdir(path)` | Creates a folder and its parents. |
| `node.fs.remove(path, recursive)` | Deletes a file or an empty folder; a folder with contents only with `recursive = true`. |
| `node.fs.rename(from, to)` | Renames or moves, replacing the target. |
| `node.fs.copy(from, to)` | Copies a file, replacing the target. |

For paths there are `node.fs.join`, `node.fs.dirname`, `node.fs.basename` and `node.fs.extension`.

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
node.fs.mkdir("reports")
local report = node.json.encode({ ok = true }, { pretty = true })
node.fs.write("reports/today.json", report)

local back = node.json.decode(node.fs.read("reports/today.json"))
node.log("read back: %s", back.ok and "ok" or "?")

-- expect: read back: ok
```

`node.fs.write` isn't atomic: a crash mid-write leaves half a file. When that matters, write a temporary file and rename it, which replaces the old file in one step.

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function saveFile(path, data)
    local tmp = path .. ".tmp"
    if not node.fs.write(tmp, data) then return false end
    return node.fs.rename(tmp, path)
end

node.log("saved: %s", tostring(saveFile("state.json", "{}")))

-- expect: saved: true
```

For a big file whose write would hold up the worker thread, `node.fs.writeAsync(path, data, done)` writes on a background thread, then calls `done(ok)`.

## Watching a file

`node.fs.watch(path, fn)` calls `fn(path, "changed")` or `fn(path, "removed")` about a second after a change, which suits a list the host edits by hand while the server runs:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function logChange(path, what)
    node.log("%s %s", path, what)
end

node.fs.watch("notes.txt", logChange)

local function writeNotes()
    node.fs.write("notes.txt", "hello")
end

node.after(1500, writeNotes)

-- expect: notes.txt changed
```

`node.fs.watch` returns an id, and `node.fs.unwatch(id)` stops the watch. A plugin can have at most 64 watches; the next call returns `nil, "limit"`. Watches end when the plugin unloads.

---

# The db module

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/database/

> Setting up the db module, db.lua, queries with placeholders, creating tables, transactions, NULL and errors in PostgreSQL, SQLite and MySQL.

The database module ships with the server as `db.dll` or `db.so` in `modules/` and works the same with PostgreSQL, SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB. You write the SQL; the placeholders `$1`, `$2`… work on every engine, and values travel separately from the query text.

## Setting it up

The host tells the module where the database is: copy `db.example.toml` from `modules/` next to the program to `modules/db.toml` in the server's working folder and fill in the `default` connection. A `db.toml` directly in the working folder also works.

```toml
[connections.default]
driver = "postgres"
url = "postgres://node:secret@127.0.0.1/node"
connections = 4
```

| Key | Default | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `driver` | from `url` | `postgres`, `sqlite` or `mysql`. Without it, `url` decides: `postgres://`, `postgresql://` or a `host=… dbname=…` string is PostgreSQL, `mysql://` or `mariadb://` is MySQL, anything else SQLite. |
| `url` | none | The database address. For SQLite, a file path from the server's folder, such as `"data/server.db"`; `":memory:"` is an in-memory database that is gone when the server stops. |
| `connections` | `4` | The pool size, from 1 to 32: how many queries can run at once. |
| `query_timeout_ms` | `10000` | How long one query may run. |
| `tx_timeout_ms` | `30000` | How long a transaction may stay open, including the wait for a free connection. |
| `max_rows` | `10000` | A result with more rows fails with `db_result_cap`. |

The module reads the file once, at startup. To keep the password out of the file, set `NODE_DB_DEFAULT_URL`: it replaces the file's address (`NODE_DB_<NAME>_URL` for a connection with another name). Without a file the module takes `NODE_DB_URL`. With no connection configured, the module logs `no database configured` at startup and answers every request with `db_disabled`.

## db.lua in a plugin

Plugins reach the module through `db.lua`, a small library in `modules/` next to the module. Copy it into the plugin's `server/` folder and load it:

<!-- doctest: skip the doctest runner puts these lines in front of every db block -->
```lua
local here = debug.getinfo(1, "S").source:sub(2):match("^(.*)[/\\]")
package.path = here .. "/?.lua;" .. package.path
local db = require("db").open()
```

`open()` takes the `default` connection, `open("stats")` another one from `db.toml`. Call with a colon, `db:query(...)`: the library rejects a call with a dot and says why. After a server update, copy the new `db.lua` over the old one.

## Queries

| Call | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `db:query(sql, params)` | `{ rows, count, columns }`, or `nil, err`. Each row in `rows` is a column = value table. |
| `db:exec(sql, params)` | How many rows changed, or `nil, err`. For `insert`, `update` and `delete`. |
| `db:ready()` | `true` once the connection is up. |
| `db:status()` | One table with the driver, state and counters of every connection. |

Inside `node.async` the calls wait and return the answer. With a function as the last argument, the call returns at once and later calls it with `(result, err)`.

A plugin usually creates its tables at startup, when the connection may not be up yet, so wait for it:

<!-- doctest: db -->
```lua
local function createTable()
    while not db:ready() do
        node.sleep(500)
    end
    local _, err = db:exec([[
        create table if not exists visits (
            account bigint primary key,
            times integer not null
        )]])
    if err then
        return node.log.error("%s: %s", err.code, err.message)
    end
    node.log("visits table ready")
end

node.async(createTable)

-- expect: visits table ready
```

A visit counter: one statement inserts the first visit or adds one, another reads the count.

<!-- doctest: db+client -->
```lua
local function recordVisit(player)
    local _, err = db:exec([[
        insert into visits (account, times) values ($1, 1)
        on conflict (account) do update set times = visits.times + 1
    ]], { player.accountId })
    if err then
        return node.log.error("%s: %s", err.code, err.message)
    end
    local res = db:query("select times from visits where account = $1",
        { player.accountId })
    player:tell("Visit number %d", res.rows[1].times)
end

local function onJoined(player)
    if not player.accountId then return end
    node.async(recordVisit, player)
end

node.on("playerJoined", onJoined)

-- expect-client: Alice chat:msg .*Visit number \d+
```

## Transactions

`db:tx(fn)` holds one connection for all of `fn`, and inside it `tx:query` and `tx:exec` always wait for the answer. When `fn` returns, the changes are committed; if it raises an error or calls `tx:rollback(reason)`, they are undone. `db:tx` returns what `fn` returned, or `nil, err`. After a rollback `err.code` is `"rollback"` and what `fn` raised is in `err.cause`.

<!-- doctest: db -->
```lua
local function transfer(from, to, cents)
    local function move(tx)
        local res, err = tx:query(
            "select cents from wallets where account = $1", { from })
        if err then error(err) end
        local have = res.rows[1] and res.rows[1].cents or 0
        if have < cents then
            return tx:rollback("not enough money")
        end
        tx:exec("update wallets set cents = cents - $1 where account = $2",
            { cents, from })
        tx:exec("update wallets set cents = cents + $1 where account = $2",
            { cents, to })
        return true
    end
    return db:tx(move)
end

local function runTransfers()
    while not db:ready() do
        node.sleep(500)
    end
    db:exec([[create table if not exists wallets (
        account bigint primary key, cents bigint not null)]])
    db:exec([[insert into wallets values (1, 1000), (2, 0)
        on conflict do nothing]])
    local ok, err = transfer(1, 2, 500)
    node.log("first transfer: %s", tostring(ok))
    ok, err = transfer(1, 2, 5000)
    node.log("second transfer: %s", err and err.message or "done")
end

node.async(runTransfers)

-- expect: first transfer: true
-- expect: second transfer: not enough money
```

The module rolls back a transaction open longer than `tx_timeout_ms`, so a forgotten one can't hold a connection forever. If the plugin reloads or stops mid-transaction, the connection is freed at once.

## NULL and other values

A parameter list is a Lua array, where a `nil` would end it early, so write `db.NULL` for SQL NULL. The library rejects a list with a gap; to keep a gap, give the length: `{ a, nil, b, n = 3 }` sends the `nil` as NULL.

<!-- doctest: skip shows only the parameter list -->
```lua
db:exec("insert into notes (id, text) values ($1, $2)", { 7, db.NULL })
```

A table in the parameters is sent as JSON, for `json` or `jsonb` columns.

## Errors

Errors are returned, not raised, as `{ code, message, detail, constraint, … }`. The code is a SQLSTATE, the same on every engine for the same error, or the module's own code starting with `db_`:

| Code | What it means |
|---|---|
| `23505` | Duplicate unique key; `constraint` names it if the engine reports the name. |
| `23503`, `23502`, `23514` | A foreign key, NOT NULL or CHECK violation. |
| `42601`, `42P01` | A syntax error; no such table. |
| `40001`, `40P01` | A serialization failure; a deadlock. |
| `57014` | The query ran longer than `query_timeout_ms`. |
| `08001`, `08006` | No connection; the connection was lost. |
| `db_disabled` | No connection by that name, or the module isn't configured. |
| `db_queue_full` | 1000 statements are already queued. |
| `db_tx_timeout` | The transaction ran longer than `tx_timeout_ms`. |
| `db_tx_aborted` | The module rolled the transaction back because its plugin unloaded. |
| `db_result_cap` | More rows than `max_rows`. |
| `db_params` | The parameter list or the SQL is unusable. |

---

# HTTP requests

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/http/

> Callbacks and coroutines, errors, a Discord webhook, certificates and why requests to local addresses are refused.

`node.http` sends HTTP and HTTPS requests from a plugin. They run on background threads and answer on the worker thread, so a slow service doesn't hold up the server.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node.http.get(url, headers, cb)` | GET. |
| `node.http.post(url, body, headers, cb)` | POST. A table body is sent as JSON. |
| `node.http.request(method, url, opts, cb)` | Any method; `opts = { headers, body }`. |
| `node.http.put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head` | The same with a fixed method. |
| `node.http.fetch(url, opts)` | Inside `node.async`, waits for the answer and returns it. |

`headers` is optional. The callback gets `(status, body, headers)`. A request takes at most about 15 seconds, and an answer can be up to 8 MB. The server follows up to five redirects, but not from `https` to `http` while certificates are checked. The call returns `false` if the request couldn't be queued, and the callback is then never called.

## Errors

If a request fails before an answer (no connection, a bad certificate, a timeout), `status` is `-1` and `body` says why, as a refused request shows:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function logAnswer(status, body)
    if status == -1 then
        node.log("failed: %s", body)
    else
        node.log("answer %d, %d bytes", status, #body)
    end
end

node.http.get("http://127.0.0.1:9/", logAnswer)

-- expect: failed: .*blocked
```

Requests to the server's own machine and private networks are refused by default ([below](#local-and-private-addresses)), which is why this one fails.

## Waiting in a coroutine

Inside `node.async`, `node.http.fetch` waits for the answer and returns it, so several requests in a row read top to bottom:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function fetchStatus()
    local status = node.http.fetch("http://127.0.0.1:9/")
    node.log("status %d", status)
end

node.async(fetchStatus)

-- expect: status -1
```

`fetch` takes `{ method = "POST", body = ..., headers = ... }` as its second argument. If the request couldn't be queued, `status` is `0` and `body` is `request not queued`.

## A Discord webhook

This plugin posts to a Discord channel when a player joins. The webhook address is a secret, so it goes in `[config]`, not in the code:

<!-- doctest: skip needs a real Discord webhook address -->
```lua
local webhook = node.config.webhook

local function warnOnFailure(status, body)
    if status ~= 204 then
        node.log.warn("webhook answered %d: %s", status, body)
    end
end

local function announceJoin(player)
    local message = { content = player.name .. " joined the server" }
    node.http.post(webhook, message, warnOnFailure)
end

node.on("playerJoined", announceJoin)
```

## Certificates

The server checks HTTPS certificates against the system's trusted roots and the `cacert.pem` shipped with the server; a host can point `[http] ca_file` at their own bundle. `[http] insecure` turns the check off. Don't turn it on: anyone between the server and the service could then read and change what you send.

## Local and private addresses

A plugin can't reach the server's own machine, the local network or other private addresses unless the host sets `[http] allow_private_networks = true`. That keeps plugins away from services that must not be exposed. If, say, a statistics service runs next to the game server, the host can turn the key on, but private addresses then open to every plugin on the server.

---

# The bus between plugins

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/bus/

> How plugins on one server send each other messages, how to name them, parse the data, ask and answer, and what else travels on the bus.

Plugins can't see each other's variables ([How a plugin is built](/plugins/resources/#the-lua-environment)), so they talk over the bus, a publish-subscribe channel inside the server: one plugin publishes a message under a name, and every plugin subscribed to that name gets it.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node.bus.emit(name, data)` | Publishes `data` under `name`. A table becomes JSON. |
| `node.bus.call(name, data)` | Asks every plugin subscribed to `name` and returns their answers at once. |
| `node.bus.on(name, fn)` | Calls `fn(source, data)` for every message under `name`. |
| `node.bus.off(name, fn)` | Unsubscribes; without `fn`, all of this plugin's handlers for `name`. |

`source` is the sending plugin's name, `"native"` for a native module. `data` arrives as a string; parse it with `node.json.decode`.

## Sending and receiving

The `scores` plugin keeps the tally:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local scores = {}

local function addScore(source, data)
    local add = node.json.decode(data)
    scores[add.name] = (scores[add.name] or 0) + add.points
    node.log("%s: %s +%d = %d", source, add.name, add.points, scores[add.name])
end

node.bus.on("score:add", addScore)

-- expect: \S+: Alice \+10 = 10
```

Any other plugin awards points:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function awardPoints()
    node.bus.emit("score:add", { name = "Alice", points = 10 })
end

node.after(500, awardPoints)
```

The server delivers a message on the worker thread after the current handler finishes, not in the middle of it, and the sender gets it too if subscribed. Name messages `<plugin>:<what>`, like wire events, so two plugins don't collide ([Events](/plugins/events/#kinds-of-events)).

## Asking and answering

`node.bus.call` asks a question and gets the answers at once; a handler answers with its return value:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function answerPrice(source, data)
    return { item = data, cents = 250 }
end

node.bus.on("shop:price", answerPrice)
```

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function askPrice()
    for _, a in ipairs(node.bus.call("shop:price", "wrench")) do
        node.log("%s asks %d cents", a.source, a.value.cents)
    end
end

node.after(500, askPrice)

-- expect: \S+ asks 250 cents
```

- All handlers run immediately, before `call` returns, so the answer is what the other plugin knows at that moment.
- Answers come as a list of `{ source, value }` in subscription order, a table as a table. A handler that returns `nil` is left out, so an empty list means nobody answered.
- The asking plugin's own handlers get the question too.
- A handler can itself `call`, at most eight levels deep; beyond that `call` raises an error.
- A native module subscribed to the name sees the question but can't answer it.

A handler that must wait for something, such as a database or an HTTP request, can't answer with `return`. Put a reply name in the question and answer later with `emit`:

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function answerBalance(source, data)
    local ask = node.json.decode(data)
    node.bus.emit(ask.replyTo, { cents = 1500 })
end

node.bus.on("bank:ask", answerBalance)
```

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local me = node.resources.manifest().name

local function logBalance(_, data)
    node.log("balance: %d cents", node.json.decode(data).cents)
end

node.bus.on("bank:balance:" .. me, logBalance)

local function askBalance()
    node.bus.emit("bank:ask", { replyTo = "bank:balance:" .. me })
end

node.after(500, askBalance)

-- expect: balance: 1500 cents
```

A reply name with the asking plugin's name in it keeps replies apart. To wait for the reply in a coroutine, use `node.suspend`, which turns a callback into a pause ([Timers and coroutines](/plugins/concurrency/#coroutines)), as the database module's `db.lua` does.

## What else travels on the bus

- `player:tell` and `node.chat.say` publish `chat:say`, and the server shows it in chat.
- [The db module](/plugins/database/) answers plugins over the bus.
- Native modules also send and receive bus messages ([Native modules](/plugins/native-modules/)).

---

# Client scripts

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/client-scripting/

> How client files reach the game, engine files and extensions, talking to the server, files inside the car, session settings and strict sessions.

Everything in a plugin's `client/` folder goes to every player on joining and runs in their BeamNG.drive. The player installs nothing, and the client mod unloads these scripts when the player leaves the server.

## How files reach the game

- The server packs the client files once, at startup: every `.lua` file in `client/`, or those listed in `[client] files`. It checks their syntax and obfuscates them ([Plugins on the server](/hosting/resources/#obfuscating-client-scripts)). A syntax error goes to the server log, but the file still ships.
- The server sends the files to a player right after the map name, and they run while the map is still loading.
- The server skips a file larger than 900 KB after packing, with a warning in the log. The mod takes at most 512 files and 8 MB from one plugin and drops a plugin over either limit whole.
- The mod accepts a plugin name of up to 128 characters: Latin letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or a digit. It rejects a plugin with any other name.
- A file path may have up to 256 characters, the same ones plus `/`, and no `..`; the mod skips a file with any other path.
- The mod compiles the files in memory and writes nothing to the player's disk.

Errors on the player's side go to their own `beamng.log`, not to the server. While developing, set `[client] obfuscation = "none"` to keep that log readable.

## Game-engine files

Every client file outside `lua/vehicle/` runs in the game engine, with the game's own Lua API. Such a file is a module: it runs once, and what it returns is what the plugin's other files get from `require`; `require("ui")` loads `client/ui.lua`.

A file that returns a table with `on…` functions becomes a game extension, and the game calls them as for any extension, `onUpdate(dt)` every frame included.

<!-- doctest: client -->
```lua
local M = {}

local secondsLeft = 0

local function startCountdown(data)
    secondsLeft = jsonDecode(data).countdown
end

node.on("race:start", startCountdown)

function M.onUpdate(dt)
    if secondsLeft <= 0 then return end
    secondsLeft = secondsLeft - dt
    ui_message(string.format("Start in %d", math.ceil(secondsLeft)), 1, "race")
end

return M
```

## Extensions and the mod script

A file under `client/lua/ge/extensions/` becomes an extension named as the game names that path: `client/lua/ge/extensions/race/hud.lua` is `race_hud`. As after `extensions.load`, it becomes a global of that name, the extensions in its `M.dependencies` load first, and its `on…` functions get the game's events.

<!-- doctest: client -->
```lua
-- client/lua/ge/extensions/race/hud.lua
local M = {}

M.dependencies = { "race_core" }

function M.onExtensionLoaded()
    ui_message("Laps: " .. race_core.laps(), 5, "race")
end

return M
```

### Which files run

Without a mod script every file runs in arrival order: by path, with files directly in `lua/ge/extensions/` first, or in the order of `[client] files`. An extension's dependencies still run before it.

### The mod script

To choose what loads, put a mod script at `client/scripts/<name>/modScript.lua` or `client/modScript.lua`, as in an ordinary game mod. It runs first, and only what it loads runs:

<!-- doctest: client -->
```lua
-- client/scripts/race/modScript.lua
setExtensionUnloadMode("race_core", "manual")
setExtensionUnloadMode("race_hud", "manual")
loadManualUnloadExtensions()
```

`load`, `extensions.load`, `setExtensionUnloadMode` with `loadManualUnloadExtensions`, and `registerCoreModule` load the plugin's own extension of that name. Extensions marked `"manual"` load in the order marked (here `race_core`, then `race_hud`), even if the script forgets `loadManualUnloadExtensions()`. Several mod scripts run in path order.

### Mods from the content folder

A name the plugin doesn't have belongs to the game, such as an extension of a mod in the server's `content/` folder; that mod needs no `scripts/` folder of its own. The client mod loads the extension when the plugin arrives and, if it wasn't loaded before the plugin, unloads it when the player leaves.

<!-- doctest: client -->
```lua
-- client/modScript.lua
load("race_core")      -- the plugin's: client/lua/ge/extensions/race/core.lua
load("bigmap_sounds")  -- the game's: an extension of a mod in content/
```

## Talking to the server

A client file has a `node` table of its own, smaller than the server's:

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node.on(name, fn [, source])` | Calls `fn(data)` for a wire event from the server. `data` arrives as a string. An optional `source` lets multiple files of the plugin subscribe to the same event. |
| `node.off(name [, source])` | Unsubscribes (all of the plugin's handlers for `name`, or only `source`). |
| `node.emitServer(name, data)` | Sends a wire event to the server. `data` must be a string. |
| `node.log(text)` | Writes to the game's `beamng.log`. |

By default on the client a plugin has one handler per event name: another `node.on` without a third `source` argument replaces it, even from another file of the plugin. Pass a `source` string as the third argument to keep separate handlers across files; all of them are removed when the plugin unloads.

The server side of the same conversation:

<!-- doctest: server+client {"emit": [["race:ready", "{\"car\": \"pickup\"}"]]} -->
```lua
local function startRace(player, data)
    local ready = node.json.decode(data)
    node.log("%s is ready in a %s", player.name, ready.car)
    player:send("race:start", { countdown = 5 })
end

node.on("race:ready", startRace)

-- expect: Alice is ready in a pickup
-- expect-client: Alice race:start .*"countdown":5
```

`player:send` and `node.broadcast` turn a table into JSON; on the client the game's `jsonDecode` parses it, and `jsonEncode` encodes a table for `node.emitServer`. What a client sends reaches only the server; for other players to see it, the server half must pass it on.

The plugin's `node.on` handlers are removed when the player leaves the server. The client mod's `NodeMP.events.on` and `NodeMP.events.triggerServer` parse and encode JSON themselves; they are meant for ordinary game mods and stay subscribed after the session.

## Files that run inside the car

A file from `client/lua/vehicle/` doesn't run in the game engine. The client mod inserts it into the Lua of every car the player drives (when the plugin arrives and on every spawn) and runs it there once.

Inside a car, the client mod's car API takes the place of the `node` table:

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `NodeMP.vehicle.isLocal()` | `true` if this player's game simulates the car. |
| `NodeMP.vehicle.id()` | The car's id in this game. |
| `NodeMP.electrics.get(name)` | An electrics value: `"rpm"`, `"lights"`, `"gear"` … |
| `NodeMP.keys.onPressed(key, fn)` | Calls `fn` when the key is pressed. |
| `NodeMP.events.triggerServer(name, data)` | Sends a wire event to the server; a table goes as JSON. |

<!-- doctest: client -->
```lua
-- client/lua/vehicle/ready.lua
if NodeMP.vehicle.isLocal() then
    NodeMP.events.triggerServer("race:car", { id = NodeMP.vehicle.id() })
end
```

A car can send but not receive: server events arrive in the game engine. Scripts inserted into a car can't be removed cleanly, and the client mod logs a warning about it when the plugin arrives. Keep them short and ship anything bigger as a mod in `content/`.

## Settings for the session

When a player joins, the client mod sends `modules:request`, and a plugin can answer with `modules:manifest`. With the `settings` module a plugin fixes some of the player's settings for the session: they show *Set by the server* and return to the player's values after the player leaves.

<!-- doctest: server+client {"emit": [["modules:request", ""]]} -->
```lua
local function answerModulesRequest(player)
    player:send("modules:manifest", { modules = {
        nametags = { enabled = true, config = { maxDistance = 40 } },
        settings = { config = { ["nodemp.chat.visibleLines"] = 4 } },
    } })
end

node.on("modules:request", answerModulesRequest)

-- expect-client: Alice modules:manifest .*maxDistance
```

`settings` can fix `nodemp.nametags.keepVisible`, `nodemp.nametags.maxLength`, `nodemp.chat.visibleLines`, `nodemp.chat.fadeSeconds`, `nodemp.chat.timestamps`, `nodemp.hud.showPlayerIds` and four for scheduled changes: `nodemp.schedule.applyWhen`, `nodemp.schedule.interval`, `nodemp.schedule.stopSpeed` and `nodemp.schedule.stopTime`. The `nametags` module takes `style`, `maxDistance`, `fadeStart`, `fadeDistance`, `showDistance`, `hideOwn`, `showEmpty` and `hideBehindObjects`.

## Strict sessions

`player:send("session:config", { strict = true })` puts the player in a strict session: no free camera, no switching into cars the server didn't seat them in, no console or editor, local mods off. The mod undoes pause and slow motion, allows node grabbing only on foot and in first person, and reports to the server resets, recoveries, teleports and game files replaced in the user folder. `{ strict = false }` ends the session. A `session:config` without a `strict` key changes nothing, and one that arrives before the session starts applies when it starts.

Instead of `true` you can pass a table with details:

| Key | What it means | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `actions` | A list of input actions to turn off; an empty list turns off none. | The mod's set |
| `photoMode` | Who may use photo mode: `"admins"`, `"all"` or `"none"`. | `"admins"` |
| `canPhoto` | Whether this player may use photo mode when `photoMode` is `"admins"`. | `false` |
| `nodeGrab` | `"walking"` allows node grabbing only on foot, `"off"` allows it nowhere. | `"walking"` |
| `heartbeatMs` | How often the mod reports to the server, from 500 to 60000 ms. | `2000` |

In a strict session the mod sends the server wire events: `rp:strict.heartbeat` every `heartbeatMs`, with `seq`, `filtersHash`, `filtersCount`, `camera`, `vehicleId`, `walking`, `timeScale` and `checksum`, and `rp:strict.violation` with `kind` and `details` for each breach it notices. A plugin judges by these reports. On the server, `player:setStrict(true)` adds to the strict session: the server stops forwarding to others the player's camera frames aimed at a car the player isn't in.

## Binary data

For a stream too heavy for JSON there are numbered binary channels: a channel number is an integer from 0 to 4294967295, and the bytes go as they are. On the client these are `node.sendModule(channel, bytes)` and `node.onModule(channel, fn)`, on the server `node.modules.on(channel, fn)` and `node.modules.send(player, channel, bytes)`.

---

# API conventions

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/conventions/

> How API calls report failure, what happens to errors in handlers, which ids last, how to check versions and measure a plugin's memory and time.

A few rules hold across the whole API; with them you won't need the reference for every call.

## How calls report failure

- An action returns `true` or `false`: `player:kick` returns `false` if there is no such player.
- A call that can fail in several ways returns `nil` and a short reason: `player:spawnVehicle` gives `nil, "max_cars"`, `node.fs.stat` gives `nil, "not found"`.
- A read returns `nil` when there is nothing to read: `node.players.find` for an unknown name, `vehicle:transform()` before the first position.
- A call raises an error only when misused, for example with a handler that is not a function. The error points at your line.

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local ok, why = node.players.get(999):verify("size")
node.log("verify: %s (%s)", tostring(ok), tostring(why))

-- expect: verify: nil \(unknown player\)
```

## Errors in handlers

The server logs an error in a handler, timer or coroutine with the plugin's name, file, line and traceback. The first line says where it happened:

| Where | The line starts with |
|---|---|
| An event that passes only a player or a car, and a request | `error in builtin 'playerJoined'` |
| An event with data: a notification, `playerLeft` | `error in event 'vehicleEdited'` |
| A wire event | `error in event 'greeter:hello'` |
| A bus message | `error in resource event 'score:add'` |
| A bus request (`node.bus.call`) | `error in resource call 'shop:price'` |
| A timer | `error in timer callback` |
| A coroutine | `error in async task` |
| The top level of `main.lua` while loading | `error in '<path to main.lua>'` |

An error ends only that call: the plugin's other handlers keep working, and this one runs again on the next event. So skip the `pcall` around a whole handler, but check what it relies on, such as the player having an `accountId`.

## Which ids last

| Id | How long it lives |
|---|---|
| `player.id` | The session. Freed when the player leaves, then given to the next one. |
| `vehicle.id` | Until the server restarts; never reused before that. |
| `player.accountId` | For good: the same on every server and every visit. |

Store player data under `accountId`. A guest has none, and next time someone else may take the guest's name.

## Versions

| Call | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `node.server.version()` | The server's version. |
| `node.server.protoVersion()` | The wire protocol version the server speaks. |

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local version = node.server.version()
node.log("server %s, protocol %d", version, node.server.protoVersion())

-- expect: server \S+, protocol \d+
```

To call a function only where it exists, test for it: `if node.server.shutdown then … end`. Compare the protocol version with `protoVersion()`, not a number in your code. The server itself disconnects a client mod that names another protocol version in `session:hello`.

## Memory and time

Two calls show what a plugin costs:

- `node.server.memory()` returns `{ lua, luaAll, process }` in bytes: this plugin's Lua state, all plugins' states together, and the whole server.
- `node.server.handlerStats()` shows how long this plugin's handlers run: `count` runs, `min`, `max`, `mean` and `stddev` in milliseconds, and `over`, the runs that took longer than 250 ms.

<!-- doctest: server -->
```lua
local function reportUsage()
    local mem = node.server.memory()
    local stats = node.server.handlerStats()
    node.log("lua %d KB, %d runs, slowest %s ms",
        mem.lua // 1024, stats.count, tostring(stats.max))
end

node.after(1000, reportUsage)

-- expect: lua \d+ KB, \d+ runs
```

A `lua` figure that grows all evening points at a table nobody empties. A `max` creeping toward 250 ms is a reason to split the handler or move it into a coroutine ([Timers and coroutines](/plugins/concurrency/)).

---

# Native modules

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/native-modules/

> The three exported functions, ABI versions, threads, what only a native module can do, language hosts and installing a module.

A native module is a library (`.dll` on Windows, `.so` on Linux) in the `modules/` folder next to the server program. It talks to the server through `NodeApi`, a table of C functions declared in one header, `node.h`. Modules load before plugins.

Write a module when Lua can't keep up: code that runs for every packet, or a library that exists only in C. For game rules and commands a Lua plugin is simpler and safer: an error in Lua is a log line, while an error in a module can take the server down.

## The three functions

A module exports exactly three functions:

| Function | When the server calls it |
|---|---|
| `node_plugin_abi()` | First, before anything else: which ABI version the module was built for. |
| `node_plugin_init(api)` | Once, at load. `0` loads the module, any other value refuses it. |
| `node_plugin_shutdown()` | When the server stops. |

A module that greets every player in the log:

```c
#include "node.h"
#include <stdio.h>

static const NodeApi* api;

static void on_joined(int player_id, void* user) {
    char name[64], line[128];
    if (api->get_player_name(player_id, name, sizeof name) < 0) return;
    snprintf(line, sizeof line, "hello, %s", name);
    api->log_info(line);
}

NODE_PLUGIN_ABI()

NODE_EXPORT int node_plugin_init(const NodeApi* a) {
    api = a;
    api->register_builtin_event("playerJoined", on_joined, NULL);
    return 0;
}

NODE_EXPORT void node_plugin_shutdown(void) {
    api->unregister_builtin_event("playerJoined", on_joined, NULL);
}
```

`node.h` is a single C header with no import library and none of the server's internals. Any C or C++ compiler works. On Windows, build with the static C runtime so the DLL needs nothing next to it.

## ABI versions

The ABI version is `major.minor`, set by `NODE_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR` and `NODE_ABI_VERSION_MINOR` in `node.h`. `NodeApi` is a structure read by offsets, so its layout is a contract: new functions are only appended, which raises the minor version.

| The module was built | What the server does |
|---|---|
| With a different major version | Refuses to load it before the module touches anything: `module '…' was built against SDK ABI <major>.<minor>, this server speaks <major>.<minor> -- refusing to load it. Rebuild the module.` |
| With an older minor version | Loads it: everything the module knows is where it expects. |
| With a newer minor version | Loads it with a warning: the module may call functions this server doesn't have. If it must also work on such a server, check `api->struct_size` before calling a new function. |

Lua and JavaScript plugins don't need rebuilding when the server is updated.

## Return values

- An action returns `0` on success and `-1` on failure. A question returns `1` for yes and `0` for no.
- A function that fills a buffer returns the number of bytes written, or `-1` if the buffer is too small. With a `NULL` buffer it returns the length it needs, without the terminating zero.

## Threads

- Any `NodeApi` function can be called from any thread, including the module's own.
- Callbacks (events, timers, jobs, HTTP, the bus) run on the server's single worker thread, one at a time, like Lua handlers. Blocking in one holds up all plugins ([Timers and coroutines](/plugins/concurrency/)).
- The log sink (`set_log_sink`) runs on the thread that wrote the line, and must not block.
- The relay filter runs on network threads, for every packet, and must be a fast function of the module's own data. It must not change the server's state.
- The server runs the work function of `submit_job` on a background thread and calls you back on the worker thread.

## What only a module can do

- Filter the relay on the hot path. The server asks the filter from `register_relay_filter` whether one player may see another's packet, and remembers the answer. Lua can do this too, but a module answers without leaving the network thread.
- Run another language. `register_language_host` claims a plugin `type`: the server hands such plugins to the module, which loads and runs them; that is how `js-host` runs `type = "js"` ([JavaScript plugins](/plugins/js-host/)). A Lua 5.4 host can give plugins the server's own sandbox with the sdk's `lua_sandbox.hpp`, and `is_resource_trusted` says whether a plugin is listed in `[resources] trusted`.
- Suppress log lines. The log sink set with `set_log_sink` sees every line and may drop it. The server has one sink: the next `set_log_sink` replaces the previous one.

Modules talk to plugins over the [bus](/plugins/bus/) (`emit_resource_event`, `register_resource_event`, where they appear as `"native"`), and to their own client halves over numbered binary channels (`register_module_channel`, `send_module`). A module can also ask plugins: `call_resource_event` runs their handlers at once and passes each answer to a callback before returning; call it from a callback, on the worker thread. A module subscribed to the name sees such a question but can't answer it ([The bus between plugins](/plugins/bus/#asking-and-answering)). A module can't add functions to Lua: whatever it offers plugins goes over the bus, as with the [db module](/plugins/database/).

## Installing a module

Installing a module on a server: [Plugins on the server](/hosting/resources/#native-modules). At startup the server logs `<file> initialized` for each module it loads and the reason for each one it refuses.

Every function is described in the [C API reference](/plugins/api/c/).

---

# JavaScript plugins

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/js-host/

> What JavaScript plugins need, a first plugin, how the API looks from JavaScript, refusing requests, npm packages and what only Lua can do.

With the `js-host` native module installed, a plugin can be written in JavaScript and run on Node.js, with Node's own modules and npm packages. That suits bookkeeping, reports, links to other services and tasks npm already has a library for. Game rules are simpler in Lua.

## What it needs

`js-host` isn't in the server archive: it is built from source, on Windows only, with Node.js built as a library. Put `js-host.dll` in `modules/` and `libnode.dll` next to the server program, then start the server. The log shows:

```text
js-host: resources with type = "js" will run on Node
```

Without the module the server skips a JavaScript plugin and logs `resource type 'js' has no language host loaded, skipping`.

## First plugin

```toml
name = "hello-js"
type = "js"

[server]
main = "server/main.js"
```

```js
'use strict';

node.log(`${resource.name} loaded`);

function greet(playerId) {
    const name = node.getPlayerName(playerId);
    node.log(`${name} joined`);
}

node.onBuiltin('playerJoined', greet);

function countPlayers() {
    node.log(`${node.getPlayerCount()} online`);
}

const timer = node.setInterval(countPlayers, 60_000);

function stopTimer() {
    node.clearTimer(timer);
}

module.exports.unload = stopTimer;
```

The file runs once, like `main.lua`. Besides Node's globals it gets `node`, the server, and `resource` with the plugin's `name` and folder `dir`. `module.exports.unload` runs before the plugin reloads or the server stops.

## The API from JavaScript

The calls mirror the server's API one to one, named as in Lua's [`node.raw`](/plugins/api/raw/): ids go in, and a record comes back as a parsed object. There are no `Player` or `Vehicle` objects.

| Lua | JavaScript | Handler arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `node.on("playerJoined", fn)` | `node.onBuiltin('playerJoined', fn)` | `(playerId)` |
| `node.on("vehicleEdited", fn)` | `node.onVehicle('vehicleEdited', fn)` | `(playerId, vehicleId, data)` |
| `node.on("vehicleSpawnRequest", fn)` | `node.onRequest('vehicleSpawnRequest', fn)` | `(playerId, vehicleId, data)` |
| `node.on("race:finish", fn)`, a wire event | `node.on('race:finish', fn)` | `(playerId, data)` |
| `node.bus.on(name, fn)` | `node.onResource(name, fn)` | `(source, data)` |
| `node.bus.emit(name, data)` | `node.emitResource(name, string)` | |
| `player.name`, `player:kick(reason)` | `node.getPlayerName(id)`, `node.kickPlayer(id, reason)` | |
| `player:send(name, data)` | `node.emitClient(id, name, string)` | |
| `node.after`, `node.every` | `node.setTimeout(fn, ms)`, `node.setInterval(fn, ms)`, `node.clearTimer(id)` | |

The send calls take strings, so encode objects with `JSON.stringify`; a handler gets the string as sent and parses it with `JSON.parse`. `node.off(id)` removes a subscription by the id its `on…` call returned.

## Refusing a request

A request handler refuses by returning a string, the reason the player sees, or `false` for no reason. Anything else lets the request through.

```js
function refuseCityBus(playerId, vehicleId, data) {
    const config = JSON.parse(data);
    if (config.jbm === 'citybus') return 'No buses on this server';
}

node.onRequest('vehicleSpawnRequest', refuseCityBus);
```

`js-host` waits up to two seconds for the answer and lets the request through if it is late, so keep these handlers fast.

## What only Lua can do

- Take a chat line as a command (`{ handled = true }`). From JavaScript you can only refuse a line.
- Let a player in beyond the limit ([reserved slots](/plugins/events/#reserved-slots)).

Write these parts as a small Lua plugin that talks to the JavaScript one over the [bus](/plugins/bus/).

## npm packages

`require` works as in Node: Node's own modules (`node:fs`, `node:path`, …) and packages from `node_modules` inside the plugin. Run `npm install` in the plugin's folder.

Node's networking is its own: `fetch` and `node:https` bypass `node.http`, so the host's `[http]` settings (no private addresses, the certificate bundle) don't apply to them. Mind this if the plugin calls addresses that players gave it.

## Errors

An exception in a handler is logged as `js: uncaught in handler: …`, an uncaught promise rejection as `js: unhandled promise rejection: …` with a stack, and the plugin keeps running. A plugin that breaks while loading is logged as `js: hello-js failed to load: …` and skipped.

`session-report` in the server archive is a ready-made JavaScript plugin ([The example plugins](/plugins/examples/)).

---

# The example plugins

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/examples/

> The plugins in the examples folder of the server archive, what each one shows, how to try one and which plugins are built from source.

The server archive has an `examples/` folder next to the program, and each folder in it is a ready-made plugin. `examples/README.txt` lists them too.

## What's in the folder

| Example | What it shows | What to learn from it |
|---|---|---|
| `demo-numbers` | The smallest plugin with both halves: the client sends a number once a second and the server logs it. | Checking that client scripts reach players and answer. |
| `chat-commands` | `/help`, `/me` and `/pm`: a command router on `chatMessageRequest`. | Starting your own commands. |
| `freeroam-example` | Greetings, a client event with a server answer, timers. | A small plugin of the usual kind. |
| `vehicle-cleanup` | Deleting cars nobody uses: idle ones, ones whose owner has left, and any beyond a total limit. | Rules from `[config]`. |
| `gatekeeper-example` | Refusing a join, a spawn and coupler use with a reason; watching car edits, resets, paint changes and deletions. | Refusing requests and watching notifications. |
| `seat-demo` | Seating players on request from the game console: `SeatDemo.seat(gid)`, `SeatDemo.eject()`, `SeatDemo.swap()`. | `player:seat`, `player:unseat`, `player:swapWith`. |
| `nodegrab-allow` | Allowing the experimental node grabber, which is forbidden without a plugin. | A request that is closed by default. |
| `devapi-example` | A tour of the API, one feature per client event. | Seeing a call at work before reading the reference. |
| `session-report` | Who played, for how long and in what; a JSON report. Written in JavaScript. | A ready-made [JavaScript plugin](/plugins/js-host/). Needs `js-host`. |

## Installing an example

Copy the example's folder from the archive into `resources/` and restart the server ([Install a plugin](/hosting/resources/#install-a-plugin)). Comments at the top of each example's `resource.toml` and `server/main.lua` say what it does. Only `vehicle-cleanup` takes settings from `[config]`.

## vehicle-cleanup

`vehicle-cleanup` deletes the cars the server leaves in the world ([Players and vehicles](/plugins/players-and-vehicles/#whos-who-in-a-car)). Its rules are in `[config]`, and the shipped `resource.toml` has them all commented out, so off. Uncomment the ones you want:

```toml
[config]
deleteIdleAfterSeconds = 600
deleteOnSpawnerDisconnect = true
maxWorldVehicles = 20
```

`includeUnicycles` decides whether players on foot count, and `checkIntervalMs` sets how often the rules are checked.

## nodegrab-allow

The experimental node grabber needs `[experimental] node_grab = true` in `server.toml` and a plugin that answers yes to `vehicleNodeGrabRequest`; without a handler every grab is refused. `nodegrab-allow` is that handler: change its rules to allow grabbing only for some players or cars.

## Built from source, not in the archive

Some plugins are native modules, available only as source and built with CMake:

| Plugin | What it is |
|---|---|
| `js-host` | Runs JavaScript plugins ([JavaScript plugins](/plugins/js-host/)). |
| `beammp-compat` | Runs plugins written for BeamMP unchanged ([Moving from other platforms](/plugins/migrating/#beammp-plugins-without-changes)). |
| `dimensions` | Parallel worlds: players from different dimensions don't see each other. |
| `plugin-example` | The smallest working native module, a good start for your own. |

The `db` database module is built the same way but ships with the server in `modules/` ([The db module](/plugins/database/)).

---

# Moving from other platforms

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/plugins/migrating/

> How BeamMP and KissMP ideas map to NodeMP, what the beammp-compat module runs unchanged and what has no equivalent.

If you have written plugins for BeamMP or KissMP, most of what you know still applies: a server runs Lua, reacts to players and cars, and talks to scripts in the game.

## What works differently

| What | In NodeMP |
|---|---|
| Threads | The handlers of all plugins run one after another on a single worker thread. Wait with timers and coroutines ([Timers and coroutines](/plugins/concurrency/)). |
| Handlers | A handler receives a `Player` or `Vehicle` object with fields and methods, not a number ([Players and vehicles](/plugins/players-and-vehicles/)). |
| Car ids | Each car has one id, unique on the server, whoever spawned it. |
| Cars after a player leaves | They stay in the world without an owner until a plugin such as `vehicle-cleanup` deletes them ([Players and vehicles](/plugins/players-and-vehicles/#whos-who-in-a-car)). |
| Chat | Built into the server and works without plugins. A command is a chat line that a plugin takes by returning `{ handled = true }` ([Chat and commands](/plugins/chat/)). |
| Refusal | A request handler that returns `false, "reason"` refuses, and the player sees the reason ([Events](/plugins/events/#refusing-a-request)). |
| Identity | On a server in the list NodeMP verifies each player's account, and `player.accountId` works as a key for data. |

## Where things go

| On the old platform | In NodeMP |
|---|---|
| Server plugins in `Resources/Server/<plugin>/` | `resources/<name>/`, entry point `server/main.lua` |
| Client mods in `Resources/Client/` | Zip mods in `content/`; Lua for the game in `resources/<name>/client/` |
| `ServerConfig.toml` | `server.toml` ([Settings reference](/hosting/configuration/)) |
| A plugin's own settings file | The `[config]` table in `resource.toml`, read as `node.config` |

## BeamMP concepts in NodeMP

| BeamMP | NodeMP |
|---|---|
| `onInit` | The top of `main.lua`, which runs when the plugin loads |
| `onPlayerAuth` | `playerConnectRequest`: `false, "reason"` refuses, `true` grants a reserved slot |
| `onPlayerConnecting` | `playerAuthenticated` |
| `onPlayerJoining` | `playerJoining` |
| `onPlayerJoin` | `playerJoined` |
| `onPlayerDisconnect` | `playerLeft`, with the reason |
| `onChatMessage` | `chatMessageRequest`: refuse, rewrite or take the line as a command |
| `onVehicleSpawn` | `vehicleSpawnRequest` |
| `onVehicleEdited` | `vehicleEditRequest` |
| `onVehicleDeleted` | `vehicleDeleted` |
| `onVehicleReset` | `vehicleReset` |
| `onShutdown` | `serverShutdown`; the plugin saves its data in `resourceUnload` |
| `MP.SendChatMessage` | `player:tell`, and `node.chat.say` for everyone |
| `MP.DropPlayer` | `player:kick(reason)` |
| `MP.GetPlayers`, `MP.GetPlayerName` | `node.players.all()`, `player.name` |
| `MP.IsPlayerGuest`, `MP.GetPlayerIdentifiers` | `player.guest`, `player.accountId`, `player.identifiers` |
| `MP.TriggerClientEvent` | `player:send(name, data)` or `node.broadcast` |
| `MP.TriggerGlobalEvent` | `node.bus.call`, which returns the handlers' answers, or `node.bus.emit` if no answer is needed ([The bus between plugins](/plugins/bus/#asking-and-answering)) |
| `MP.CreateEventTimer`, `MP.CancelEventTimer` | `node.every(ms, fn)`, `node.cancel(id)`; `CallStrategy.Precise` is `node.every(ms, fn, { precise = true })` |
| `onConsoleInput` | `node.console.command(name, fn)` or the `consoleInput` event for whole lines |
| `MP.Sleep` | `node.sleep(ms)` inside `node.async`, without blocking |
| `MP.GetPlayerVehicles`, `MP.RemoveVehicle` | `player:vehicles()`, `vehicle:delete()` |
| `MP.GetPositionRaw` | `vehicle:transform()` or `node.vehicles.transforms()` for all cars |
| `MP.Set(MP.Settings.MaxPlayers, n)` | `node.server.setMaxPlayers(n)` |
| `Util.JsonEncode`, `Util.JsonDecode` | `node.json.encode`, `node.json.decode` |
| `FS.*` | `node.fs.*`, within the plugin's folder |
| `TriggerServerEvent` in a client mod | `node.emitServer` or `NodeMP.events.triggerServer` |
| `AddEventHandler` in a client mod | `node.on` or `NodeMP.events.on` |

The same welcome and command as a NodeMP plugin:

<!-- doctest: server+client {"emit": [["chat:send", {"text": "/hello"}]]} -->
```lua
local function announceJoin(player)
    node.chat.say("%s joined the server", player.name)
end

node.on("playerJoined", announceJoin)

local function answerHello(player, msg)
    if msg.text ~= "/hello" then return end
    player:tell("Hello, %s!", player.name)
    return { handled = true }
end

node.on("chatMessageRequest", answerHello)

-- expect-client: Alice chat:msg .*Alice joined the server
-- expect-client: Alice chat:msg .*Hello, Alice!
```

## KissMP concepts in NodeMP

There is no KissMP compatibility module, so a KissMP plugin has to be rewritten with these equivalents:

| KissMP | NodeMP |
|---|---|
| Hooks for a player connecting and leaving | `playerConnectRequest`, `playerJoined`, `playerLeft` |
| The chat hook | `chatMessageRequest` |
| Hooks for spawning, resetting and deleting cars | `vehicleSpawnRequest`, `vehicleSpawned`, `vehicleReset`, `vehicleDeleted` |
| The per-tick hook | `serverTick`, or better a timer, `node.every(ms, fn)` |
| A connection object: name, messages, kick | `Player`: `player.name`, `player:tell`, `player:kick` |
| Cars and their positions | `node.vehicles.all()`, `node.vehicles.transforms()` |
| Data in files | `node.storage`, `node.fs` or the [db module](/plugins/database/) |
| Lua sent to players | The plugin's `client/` files ([Client scripts](/plugins/client-scripting/)) |
| Mods the server hands out | Zip archives in `content/` ([Mods and maps](/hosting/mods/)) |

## BeamMP plugins without changes

The `beammp-compat` native module runs BeamMP server plugins as they are. It is a language host that claims `type = "beammp"` and gives each such plugin the `MP`, `Util` and `FS` tables a BeamMP plugin expects.

`beammp-compat` isn't in the server archive; build it from source with CMake, like the other [native modules](/plugins/examples/#built-from-source-not-in-the-archive), and put `beammp-compat.dll` in `modules/`. Then lay the plugin out as a folder in `resources/`:

```text
resources/
└── my-plugin/
    ├── resource.toml
    ├── main.lua         ← the plugin's files, unchanged
    ├── commands.lua
    └── client/          ← the client mod's files, unpacked (optional)
```

```toml
name = "my-plugin"
type = "beammp"

[server]
main = "main.lua"
```

The file from `[server] main` runs first, then every other `.lua` file directly in the folder, alphabetically, in one Lua state as in BeamMP, then `onInit`. Name one of the files as the entry point: to the server, a folder with neither `server/main.lua` nor client files isn't a plugin.

### What runs as it is

- Every player and vehicle event from the table above, with BeamMP's arguments, plus `postPlayerAuth`, `postChatMessage`, `postVehicleSpawn` and `postVehicleEdited`.
- Custom events from clients, `MP.TriggerLocalEvent` and `MP.TriggerGlobalEvent` between plugins, timers, `MP.Get` for the player and car limits, the map and the name, and `MP.Set` for the limits and the name.
- `Util.Json*`, `Util.Random*`, `Util.Log*` and `FS.*` for files and folders.
- In the game, the client globals the BeamMP client mod calls: `TriggerServerEvent`, `TriggerClientEvent`, `AddEventHandler`, `MPGameNetwork`, `MPCoreNetwork`, `MPConfig`, `MPVehicleGE`, `UI`.

### What behaves differently

- In `onVehicleSpawn` the car id is the one the client proposed, `0` for a new car: NodeMP assigns the real id after the decision, and `postVehicleSpawn` brings it.
- `MP.SendChatMessage` shows the line as a system line.
- `MP.Sleep` blocks the worker thread, and with it every plugin; the module warns about this once.
- The identifier that BeamMP calls `beammp` is the player's NodeMP account number.
- Like any plugin, it reaches only its own folder ([The Lua environment](/plugins/resources/#the-lua-environment)); paths it builds as `Resources/Server/<plugin>/…` in `FS.*`, `io.open` and the like lead there. A plugin that reads other folders, starts programs or reads environment variables needs the host to list it in `[resources] trusted`.

### What has no equivalent

- `onConsoleInput` and `onFileChanged` never fire.
- `MP.ConfirmationDialog`, `Util.JsonDiff` and `Util.JsonDiffApply` are stubs.
- There is no `Http.CreateConnection`: a blocking HTTP request would stop the server. Use `node.http` from a Lua plugin.
- `exit()` only writes a warning: a plugin can't stop the server this way.
- In the game there are no modules for separate data streams: `MPInputsGE`, `MPElectricsGE`, `MPPowertrainGE`, `positionGE`, `MPHelpers`, `MPUpdatesGE` and `MPModManager`.

To rewrite a plugin piece by piece, put `mp.lua` and `mp_backend_node.lua` from the module's sources next to `server/main.lua` of an ordinary Lua plugin and load them with `require("mp")` ([Several files](/plugins/resources/#several-files)). The plugin gets the same `MP`, `Util` and `FS` tables, so old code and new code on `node` run in one plugin.

---

# Error messages

Source: https://docs.nodemp.com/reference/error-codes/

> Launcher notifications, the server's refusals and kicks, the helper's exit codes, and what to do about each message.

NodeMP has no error numbers. A join is stopped by a sentence: a launcher notification, a refusal or kick from the server, or the last line of the helper's log. They are all here, with `…` for a part that changes. The common cases step by step: [When something breaks](/players/troubleshooting/).

## Launcher notifications

A notification has a title that names the step and, under it, the reason; the tables write them as *title* · `reason`. Titles follow the interface language, while reasons from the helper and the server are in English. Errors and warnings stay in the notification center under the bell icon: **Copy** puts their text on the clipboard, and **Details** shows the server's or the helper's original words.

### Client mod

| Message | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| *Could not join* · `client mod is not installed and the directory is unreachable` | `NodeMP.zip` isn't on the disk yet, and NodeMP didn't answer. | Check your connection and join again. |
| *Could not join* · `client mod is not installed and no release has been published yet` | `NodeMP.zip` isn't there, and NodeMP hasn't published any version of the mod yet. | Join later. |
| *Could not join* · `could not start the download: …`, `the download server returned …`, `the download stopped: …`, `the download was N bytes, the release says M`, `the download is larger than the release says` | The mod download didn't start or broke off. | Check your connection, VPN or proxy and join again. |
| *Could not join* · `the downloaded client mod does not match the published checksum`, `the …'s signature does not verify: it was not signed by NodeMP` | The downloaded file failed the checksum or signature check, so the launcher doesn't install it. | Join again. |
| *Could not join* · `LOCALAPPDATA is not set, so BeamNG's user folder cannot be found` | Windows didn't pass the launcher the `LOCALAPPDATA` variable, which it uses to find the game's user folder. | Restart the computer. If that doesn't help, set the variable yourself; it's usually `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local`. |
| *Client mod could not be updated* · *Joining with the installed copy.* | The check failed, but the previous `NodeMP.zip` is in place, and the launcher joins with it. This is a warning. | If the server refuses the old mod, close the game and click **Settings → Game → Client mod → Check now**. |
| *Could not check the client mod* · `could not replace …\NodeMP.zip (is BeamNG.drive running?): …` | The running game holds the file. | Close BeamNG.drive and click **Check now**. |

### Starting a session

| Message | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| *Could not start the session* · `could not start …: …` | The system didn't start the helper, and its message follows the colon. | Check whether an antivirus blocks `NodeMP.exe`, or reinstall the launcher from [nodemp.com/download](https://nodemp.com/download). |
| *The launcher's traffic helper stopped* · the last line of its log | The helper ended with an error during the join or the game. | Look the line up under [Helper exit codes](#helper-exit-codes). |
| *You are already on a server: leave the game to join another* | A join was started while another session is running. | Close BeamNG.drive. |
| *Connection cancelled* | You clicked **Cancel**. | Nothing. |
| *Could not join* · *Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again to join as yourself.* | NodeMP no longer accepts the saved sign-in, and there is no join ticket. The game didn't start. | Click **Sign in** in the notification and sign in again ([Your account](/players/sign-in/)). |
| *Could not join* · *NodeMP could not be reached for a join ticket.* | NodeMP didn't answer. The game didn't start. | Click **Try again**. |
| *Could not join* · NodeMP's refusal text | NodeMP didn't issue a join ticket. Under the text there may be the advice *Try again in N s.* or a decision number to quote to support. | Follow the advice. If the server lets guests in, the notification has **Play as a guest**. |

### Connecting

| Message | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| *Could not connect* · `Could not reach the server` | Nothing answers at that address: the server is off, its port is closed, or a firewall is in the way. | Refresh the list. If it's your server, check that the port is open for TCP and UDP. |
| *Could not connect* · `DNS Lookup Failed` | The name you entered in Direct Connect can't be found. | Check the spelling or enter the IP address. |
| *Could not connect* · `server certificate fingerprint mismatch` | The server's certificate isn't the one the launcher expected: for a listed server, the one NodeMP knows; for an unlisted one, the one the launcher remembered on the first connection. | Ask the host whether they reinstalled the server. In the server card, click **Refresh and join** for a listed server or **Continue** for a direct-connect server, or delete its entry in `known_servers.json` in the launcher's cache folder. |
| *Could not connect* · `TLS handshake failed: …`, `server presented no certificate` | Something other than a NodeMP server answered, or the connection broke during the handshake. | Check the address and port and try again. Through a VPN: [A bad connection and VPNs](/players/connection/#connection-error-messages). |

### Downloading the server's mods

These reasons come in a *The server refused the join* or *Session ended* notification.

| Reason | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `Server cannot find …`, `Server refused … (protected)`, `Server failed to read …` | The server named a mod it can't or won't send. | Tell the host. |
| `Mod '…' is protected: the server does not send it, so it has to be put in the cache folder by hand: …` | The host wants players to download this mod themselves. | Get the zip from the host and put it in the folder the message names. |
| `Failed to verify "…"` | The downloaded mod didn't match what the server announced, twice. | Tell the host. If you delete the file on the **Content** tab, it downloads again. |
| `Received corrupted download confirmation, aborting download.`, `Download announcement does not match the mod list, aborting download.` | The server's answer during the download didn't add up. | Join again. If it repeats, tell the host. |

### The server list, the cache and updates

| Message | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| *Could not reach NodeMP* | The server list didn't load. The line under the title names NodeMP's address. | Check your connection and VPN. |
| *Technical work: the server list is closed for now* | NodeMP is under maintenance and issues no join tickets, so you can't join by address either; games in progress go on. | Wait: the launcher asks again by itself. |
| *Could not remove the file* · `could not remove …: …`, `… is no longer in the cache`, `… is not a cached content file` | The file wasn't removed from the **Content** tab. The first message usually means the game holds the file. | Close the game and try again. |
| *Could not install the launcher update* · `the downloaded installer does not match the published checksum`, `the …'s signature does not verify: it was not signed by NodeMP`, `the download stopped (…); it resumes on the next try`, `the download stopped at N of M bytes; it resumes on the next try` | The installer didn't download completely or failed the check. | Try again: the download resumes where it stopped. |
| `Could not find a BeamNG.drive install. Browse to it, or launch the game once so Steam writes its path.` | The game isn't found under the path in **Settings → Game**. | Click **Browse** and choose the game folder, or start the game through Steam and click **Find it**. |
| `No Bin64\BeamNG.drive.x64.exe in this folder` | The path in **Settings → Game** isn't the game's main folder. | Choose the folder that holds `Bin64\`. |

## The server's refusals and kicks

At the door, a refusal shows as *The server refused the join*. During a session, the game reports that the session ended, and the launcher comes back with *Session ended*. The server's log has the same text as `<name> kicked — <reason>`.

For version and game-file refusals, the launcher replaces the server's sentence with its own advice, often with a button; such rows say what the launcher shows, and the server's own words are under **Details**. Plugins can kick with their own text, which you see as it is.

| Reason | When | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `Protocol version mismatch: launcher speaks v22, server speaks v21 - update the outdated side` | The launcher and the server have different protocol versions; the message gives both real numbers. If the launcher is behind, it shows `This server needs a newer launcher — update now` with the **Update now** button; if the server is behind, `This server runs an older NodeMP server (protocol v21; this launcher speaks v22)`. | **Update now** updates the launcher and joins again. If the server is behind, tell the host. |
| `Your NodeMP mod is out of date for this server (it speaks wire protocol …, the server …). Reinstall it from the launcher.` | The client mod and the server have different protocol versions; the message gives both. | If the mod's number is lower, close the game, click **Settings → Game → Client mod → Check now** and join again. If it is higher, tell the host: the server is behind. |
| `Server full!` | The server is at its player limit, and you can't wait in its queue: you have no account, the launcher can't wait in a queue, the server isn't listed, or its queue is off. | Turn on **Free slots** in the list, or wait. |
| `The server is full and so is its join queue` | As many players are already waiting in the [join queue](/hosting/join-queue/) as the host allows. The launcher writes *The server is full, and so is its queue. Try again later.* | Try again later. |
| `Someone from your address is already in this server's join queue` | As many players from your address are already waiting in the queue as the host allows, one by default. Players on a shared connection all come from one address. The launcher writes *Someone on your network is already in this server's queue.* | Wait until that player gets in, or join from another connection. |
| `You did not join after your turn too often; this server's join queue is closed to you until …` | Your turn in the queue came several times, and you left before reaching the world. The word `until` is followed by the UTC time when the queue opens again. The launcher writes *You did not join when your turn came several times, so this server's queue is closed to you until …* and shows the time in your time zone. | Wait until then. You can join a server with a free slot now. |
| `The server is starting up; join again in a moment.` | The server is still loading its plugins. | Try again in a minute. |
| `Server shutdown` | The server is stopping. Everyone on it gets this. | Wait for the host to bring it back up. |
| `You are banned from this server` | Your address, account or launcher installation is on the server's ban list, and no reason is given. If the host gave one, you see it. | Ask the host. |
| `This server requires a NodeMP account: sign in to the launcher and join again` | The server doesn't let Test Drive in, and you joined without an account. | Sign in: **Settings → Account → Sign in**. Or turn on **No account needed** in the list. |
| `Your join ticket was not accepted (join ticket invalid or expired). Join again from the launcher to get a new one` | NodeMP didn't accept the one-time join ticket; the reason is in parentheses. | Join again. |
| `The server could not verify your account with the directory (…). Try again in a moment` | The server couldn't reach NodeMP to check the account. | Try again a little later. |
| `Resume rejected` | The connection broke and the launcher tried to resume the session, but the server refused: the session had already ended, or the key didn't match. | Join again. |
| `Resume rejected: too many failed attempts, try again later` | Too many failed attempts to resume a session from your address in a short time. | Wait a minute and join again. |
| `This account is banned from NodeMP` | NodeMP banned the account on all servers at once while you were playing. | See the ban window in the launcher ([Bans](/players/sign-in/#bans)). |
| `Disconnected by the NodeMP directory (…)` | NodeMP disconnected your account from the server; the reason code is in parentheses. | Join again. If it repeats, report it on Discord. |
| `Connection refused` | A plugin turned you away and gave no reason. If it gave one, you see it. | Ask the host. |
| `Your BeamNG install does not match the game's own file list (3 files differ). Verify the game's files in Steam and try again. …` | Some game files differ from the game's own list. The number is real. | Verify the game files in Steam. |
| `Your BeamNG install changed while you were playing, and this server requires it to match the game's own file list (1 file differs). …` | The same check, run during the session, found a change. | Undo what you installed and verify the game files. |
| `Game files do not match this server's reference (3 problems). userfolder:vehicles/pickup/pickup.jbeam (overlay), …` | A strict server: your game or user folder differs from the host's clean installation. Up to three examples follow. The launcher shows `Your game files do not match this server's reference (3 problems) · vehicles/pickup/pickup.jbeam`, and under it the first problem in words and a command for the full list. | [A strict server refuses you](/players/troubleshooting/#a-strict-server-refuses-you). |
| `Game files changed while you were playing and no longer match this server's reference (1 problem). …` | The strict check during the session found a change. The launcher shows `Your game files changed while you were playing and no longer match this server's reference (1 problem)`. | Put the files back as they were and join again. |
| `Your launcher checked your BeamNG install against a different reference manifest than this server uses (checked against reference manifest … but this server uses …).
